But should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, the twelfth day before the Kalends of February.

XXVIII. He confirms certain possessions of the monastery of St. Peter of Stivagium, given by the church of Hohenburg. (Lateran, January 22.)

[HUGO, *Annals of the Sacred and Canonical Order of Prémontré*, vol. II, Documents, p. CCLI.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1099A] sons GARNER, abbot of St. Peter of Stivagium, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

The principle of justice requires, and the kindness of the Apostolic See demands, that we extend more abundantly and readily the hand of our protection to persons and places assigned to the service of God and blessed Peter under regular discipline, and that we preserve and protect their rights and the benefits bestowed upon them with fatherly kindness. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and we approve, strengthen by the privilege of this present writing, and confirm what has been given to your church in perpetuity by the church of Hohenburg through the hand of our beloved daughter Herrad, abbess of that place, with the assent of her whole chapter, and duly confirmed in writing: [Col. 1099B] namely, the place of St. Gorgonius, with all things belonging to that place; and the provision for the weekly priest, namely a cartload of wine, fourteen measures of wheat, seven of barley, and twenty shillings in Strasbourg currency; and whatever is offered by hand to the same weekly priest and to your other priests when they celebrate public or private Masses in the church of Hohenburg; the benefice established at the altar of St. Odilia at Erhesheim, seventeen quarter-measures of grain; at Wolganselseim, a cartload of wine; a meadow and wood situated at St. Nabor; seventeen day-measures of land at Talheim; and permission to pasture every kind of animal in the pastures of Hohenburg. This is on the condition [Col. 1099C] that, upon the death or removal of your abbot, his successor shall receive the aforesaid benefices from the hand of the abbess of Hohenburg, by the book and without any opposition; and that he shall appoint priests of his order to serve God in that church, and both clerical and lay brethren in the aforesaid place of St. Gorgonius. Whenever your abbot wishes, he shall visit the church of Hohenburg; and each year, unless detained by illness or some evident business, he shall come to that church to celebrate solemn Mass on the feast of St. Odilia, at the dedication of the chapel, and at the Nativity of St. Mary; or, if unable to come, he shall send someone.

He shall also, by prudent arrangement, appoint in the church of Hohenburg a weekly priest and another priest to celebrate a private Mass daily at the altar [Col. 1099D] of St. Odilia, choosing whichever of his canons he knows to be suitable. The aforesaid abbot shall have full power, without opposition from the abbess, to remove them and appoint others in their places. He shall also be permitted charitably to administer, as God inspires him, the goods both spiritual and temporal belonging to the place of St. Gorgonius.

It is also established that whenever brethren or sisters depart this life, the communities of both churches shall solemnly perform a full service in Masses and the other offices. When the abbess of Hohenburg comes near to death, the abbot of Stivagium, summoned by the brethren of St. [Col. 1100A] Gorgonius, shall come quickly and, if free to do so, solemnly celebrate her obsequies in the community.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may infringe, overturn, or rashly oppose this page of our protection and confirmation. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, unless he correct his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him incur the indignation of Almighty God and His blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and be subject to divine vengeance at the last judgment. But may all who faithfully observe these provisions have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that, etc.

(Place of the sign + of Pope Lucius III.)

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1100B] I, Leodimus, bishop of Porto and of the see of St. Rufina. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St. Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title of St. Clement. I, Cynthius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Cecilia. I, Matthew, cardinal priest of the title of St. Marcellus. I, Laborantius, cardinal priest of St. Mary across the Tiber, of the title of St. Callistus. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin. I, Raynerius, cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Albert, [Col. 1100C] cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of February, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year 1181 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

(With an attached lead seal on silken cords.)

XXIX. He takes the church of St. Peter of Jovillaris under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. (Lateran, January 22.)

[HUGO, *Annals of the Sacred and Canonical Order of Prémontré*, vol. I, Documents, p. DCCXCI.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GALTER, abbot of the church of St. Mary of Royal Valley, and his brethren, present and future, [Col. 1100D] professing the regular life, forever.

It befits apostolic protection to be present for those choosing the religious life, lest perhaps an assault of any rashness either call them back from their purpose or—God forbid—break the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and, following the example of our predecessors of happy memory, Innocent, Eugenius, and Alexander, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church of St. Peter of Jovillaris, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order recognized as established in the same church according to God, the Rule of blessed Augustine, [Col. 1101A] and the Premonstratensian institution, shall be observed there inviolate in perpetuity. Furthermore, whatever possessions and whatever goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire through the Lord’s favor by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and undiminished to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to state expressly the following:

The place itself of Jovillaris, in which the abbey was founded, which you hold from Geoffrey, lord of Jovilla, with the assent of his son Jofrid, and from Matilda of Vienne, surnamed Lupa, with the assent of her son Henry and [Col. 1101B] daughter Sybilla, with all its appurtenances, lands, meadows, woods, and pastures for every kind of animal; the church and altar of Juvinicio (Juvigny), with all their appurtenances, namely endowments and tithes, offerings and alms, which our venerable brother Peter, bishop of Toul, gave you with the assent of Theodoric the archdeacon and his entire chapter; the church and altar of Savoneriis, with all their appurtenances, endowments and tithes, offerings and alms, which Guy, bishop of Châlons, gave you with the assent of his entire chapter; the portions of the freehold of that same village which you have in lands, meadows, woods, and pastures for every kind of animal; the estate of Clairfontaine which you have from the abbot and common [Col. 1101C] chapter of St. Urban, with the assent of Jofrid, advocate of that church, with all its appurtenances, lands, meadows, woods, and pastures; the place of Nantolio (Nantel), with its mill, upper pond, and other appurtenances; the freehold of Fouchers with all its appurtenances, lands, meadows, woods, serfs, and pastures for every kind of animal, which Richerius of Salamanna gave you on behalf of his daughters and wife, who had entered your church as converts, with the assent of his son Lethard and all his heirs; the mill situated near the village, with the adjoining meadow, which you have from Guy, steward of Bar, with the assent of his wife Petronilla, his sons Gerard, Lethard, and Gilo, and his daughters Alburgis and Deuvidis; the freehold which Rudolph of Asperomont, with the assent of his sons, and Robert of Solers, with the assent of all his heirs, gave you at the village [Col. 1101D] of Satana, with all its appurtenances, lands, meadows, woods, tithes, serfs, and pastures; the mill you possess within the parish of the aforesaid village, with access and exit and the course of its water, called Retucuasach; one half of another mill which you possess at Sionnam; likewise the hospital house situated near Mareium, with all its appurtenances, lands, vineyards, and the chapel built within the court of that house, together with the endowments belonging to it, which Guy, bishop of Châlons, gave you with the assent of his entire chapter. This is on the condition that your abbot shall have free power both to appoint and dismiss brethren, and charitably [Col. 1102A] to administer the goods, spiritual as well as temporal, as he sees fit and as God inspires him.

Indeed, no one shall presume to demand tithes from you on newly cleared lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the increase of your animals. You may also receive clerics and laymen who flee the world, free and unencumbered, for conversion, and retain them without any opposition. Moreover, we forbid any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, to leave it without the abbot’s permission; and no one shall dare retain one who leaves without letters of authorization from the community. We also forbid anyone to give personally, or otherwise alienate, churches, lands, or any benefice bestowed upon [Col. 1102B] your church, without the consent of the entire chapter, or its greater and sounder part. If any gifts or alienations are made otherwise than as stated, we decree them void.

Moreover, no canons or converts bound by profession to your house may, without the consent and permission of the abbot and the greater and sounder part of your chapter, give surety for anyone or borrow money from anyone beyond the amount provided by the prudent decision of their chapter, except for an evident benefit to your house. If anyone should presume to do so, the community, without whose permission and consent they acted, shall not be bound to answer in any way for these matters.

Furthermore, it shall be lawful for you in your cases to produce brethren of your own qualified to testify and, if it is accepted, by their testimony to repel violence and vindicate justice. In order to avoid the crowds of secular people, it shall be free to you, saving the right of the diocesan bishop and parish church, to construct oratories in your granges and there celebrate divine offices for yourselves and your household. For chrism, holy oil, consecrations of churches, ordinations of clerics to be promoted to sacred orders, conducting an abbot to his seat, or any other ecclesiastical sacraments, no one shall dare demand anything from you, whether under pretext of custom [Col. 1102D] or in any other manner. But should anyone presume to act contrary to this, let him know that he shall have a portion with Gehazi, whose deed he imitates by exacting a shameful gift (4 Kings 5). Furthermore, we decree that the burial place of that house shall be free, and that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; saving, nevertheless, the right of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken.

Also desiring with fatherly care to provide for your peace and tranquillity, we prohibit by apostolic authority anyone within the enclosures of your houses or granges from daring to commit violence, robbery, or theft, to set fire, or to seize [Col. 1103A] or kill a person. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things granted for the governance or support of those concerned shall be preserved whole and serve every purpose beneficial to their uses, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If, moreover, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our confirmation, should attempt obstinately to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offense by worthy satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor, recognize himself as guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject to divine vengeance at the last judgment. But may all who preserve the rights of that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theodinus, bishop of Porto and St. Rufina. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina. I, Peter, cardinal priest of St. Susanna. I, Vivian, of St. Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Cynthius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Cecilia. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title of St. Clement. [Col. 1103C] I, Arduin, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Marcus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Marcellus. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of St. Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Callistus. I, Jacob, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin. I, Rainerius, cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Ranerius, cardinal deacon of St. Adrian.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, [Col. 1103D] on the eleventh day before the Kalends of February, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year 1181 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

XXX. He confirms to the monastery of St. Augustine of Thérouanne the church of Qualquella. (Lateran, January 23.)

[MIRAEUS, *Diplomatic Works*, vol. IV, p. 377.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbot and brethren of St. Augustine of Thérouanne, greetings and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting for us readily to grant assent to the just desires of petitioners and to bring to effectual fulfillment the requests that do not depart from the path of reason [Col. 1104A].

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, meeting your just requests with favorable assent, we confirm to your devotion by apostolic authority, and strengthen by the protection of this present writing, the church of Qualquella with the tithe of grain, herrings, and other things belonging to it, as you justly and without dispute possess them. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly oppose it.

But should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

[Col. 1104B] Given at the Lateran, the tenth day before the Kalends of February.

XXXI. He takes the monastery of St. Mary of Sorø under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. (Lateran, January 25.)

[THOKHELIN, *Diplomatarium Arna-Magnaeanum*, vol. I, p. 266.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Simon, abbot of St. Mary of Sorø, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

It befits apostolic protection to be present for those choosing the religious life, lest perhaps an assault of any rashness either call them back from their purpose or [Col. 1104C]—God forbid—break the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that the monastic order which is known to have been established in that house according to God, the Rule of blessed Benedict, and the institution of the Cistercian brethren, shall be observed there unchangeably in perpetuity. Furthermore, whatever possessions and whatever goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, through the Lord’s favor, acquire by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity [Col. 1104D] of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and undiminished to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to state expressly the following:

The gift solemnly made with one purpose and harmonious devotion by our venerable brother Absalon, bishop of Roskilde, and his brother Esbern, likewise his kinsman Juno, and many others: namely, after their death, one half share of all their possessions which they had received by paternal right or added to their domains according to the law of their country; and the village called Ellingae, with its woods, pastures, and the remaining dependent settlements, which you obtained from the aforesaid venerable bishop in exchange for other lands; [Col. 1105A] likewise the village called Guthemae, which you hold partly by pious gift and partly by exchange or purchase under just title; the *mancus* at Wimmerleve; the village called Slagosae with the remaining lands belonging to it; Okelstorp; the grange at Lungae, with woods, waters, and its other appurtenances and neighboring hamlets; likewise the grange called Aswarthabothe, with woods, meadows, pastures, and the stream flowing beside it, called Tovebec, which you obtained from the aforesaid bishop in exchange for various lands; furthermore, one third of the offering which the aforesaid bishop possessed by episcopal right at the shrine of blessed Margaret in the monastery of St. Mary at Roskilde, and which he gave with the aforesaid brethren of Sorø by pious donation for the work of building the monastery or for its other uses; likewise the share of the tithe which that same bishop gave under the attestation of his privilege, namely from the parish of Fumetorp, from the parish of Sundertorp, from the parish of Eleseu, and likewise from the parish of Arclstadhe; also from the parish of Geseleve with its dependent chapel of Leoga; likewise from the parish of Swartatop; and from the parish of Berbii with the adjacent chapel of Georleve.

Indeed, no one shall presume to demand or extort tithes from you on the produce of your labor which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the increase of your animals. You may also receive clerics and laymen who flee the world, free and unencumbered, for conversion without anyone’s opposition, and retain them in your monastery.

Moreover, we forbid any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, to leave it without his abbot’s permission; and no one shall dare retain one who leaves without letters of authorization from the community. Also desiring with fatherly care to provide for your peace and tranquillity, we prohibit by apostolic authority anyone within the enclosure of your house or your granges from daring to commit violence, robbery, theft, or arson, or to seize or kill a person.

[Col. 1105D] We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, or to take away its possessions, or retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact, to be of every benefit for the use of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our confirmation, shall rashly attempt to act against it, after having been admonished a second or third time, unless he shall make amends for his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the rank of his power and honour, and know himself liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1106A] I, Theodorus, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Vivianus, cardinal priest of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of Saint Clement. I, Arduinus, cardinal priest of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary. I, Ramerius, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the [Col. 1106B] Golden Veil. I, Gratianus, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the ninth day before the Kalends of February [24 January], in the fourteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1181, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

### XXXII. To Simon, bishop of Meaux.—He confirms his statute concerning the residence of those who hold a *personatus* in the Church of Meaux. (Lateran, 29 January.)

[MARTÈNE, *Amplissima Collectio*, I, 951.]

[Col. 1106C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother S., bishop of Meaux, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Measures reasonably enacted for the benefit of Churches and for restraining the malice of those unwilling to serve the Churches from which they receive their daily stipends ought to remain firm and inviolate and, lest they be disturbed by the wickedness of evil men, ought to be strengthened by apostolic protection. We have indeed learned that those known to hold a *personatus* in your Church are unwilling to serve that Church in person; hence that Church suffers no small loss in its affairs through the absence of its officeholders. For this reason you, venerable brother, with the counsel and assent of the canons [Col. 1106D] of that Church, have reasonably decreed that no one who hereafter receives a *personatus* in that Church shall be admitted to the choir unless he has made a suitable promise to render service to the Church in his own person, while preserving nevertheless the permission of yourself and your chapter, or of its greater and sounder part. Since this constitution was reasonably made, we confirm it by apostolic authority, decreeing that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever to infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone shall presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Kalends of February [29 January].

### XXXIII. He confirms the goods and liberties of the monastery of Saint Mary of Royal Valley. (Lateran, 29 January.)

[HUGH, *Annals of Prémontré*, II, Documents, p. 412.]

[Col. 1107A]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GALTERUS, abbot of the church of Saint Mary of Royal Valley, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting that those who choose the religious life should receive apostolic protection, lest an attack of any rashness either draw them back from their purpose or, which God forbid, weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, after the example of our predecessors of happy memory, Innocent, Eugenius, and Alexander, Roman pontiffs, the aforesaid church of Saint Mary of Royal Valley, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order which is known to have been established in that church according to God, the Rule of blessed Augustine, and the institution of Prémontré shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, with the Lord’s help, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their proper terms:

[Col. 1107C] Namely, the valley itself in which the abbey was founded, from the meadow of Bovin, as the edge of the wood called Forest indicates, to the Sheep Road, which descends from Fracia below the meadow; and, on the other side, from the same meadow of Bovin, as the edge of Chelme indicates, to the spring of Beliardis, and from the spring to the road below the meadow, as the road running beside Fracia to the Granary indicates. The land of France which Guerardus and Theodoricus, lords of Sorceio, gave you with the assent of all their heirs, and through the hand of [Col. 1107D] Henry, formerly bishop of Toul, from whom they held it in fief. The allod of Bernaicuria, which they gave you, with the assent of Stephen, formerly bishop of Metz, and of Rainald, count of Bar, with its lands, woods, and pastures, together with the heirs of that allod dwelling in the following villages: namely Neves, Commarceio, Sorbeio, Meligneio, and Levovilla. The place of Bemont, formerly called Rampuns, bounded by fixed markers, namely crosses and holes made in oaks; this they gave you in lands, woods, waters, and pastures for animals of every kind, belonging to the lord of the whole territory of Commarceio: Stephania, countess of the aforesaid castle, with the assent of her son Simon and her daughters Sophia and Agnes, and of Stephen, formerly bishop of Metz, from whom she held it in fief; and Stephen of Sorceio and Savaricus of Belloramo, with the assent of his wife Mathildis; and Philip, castellan of Bar, with the assent of his sons Gerard and Ulric; and Peter, bishop of Toul, and the entire chapter of Toul.

[Col. 1108A] The mill-site which the aforesaid heirs gave you, with the lands before and behind that mill and pond, and with the watercourse necessary to it, upon the stream which runs at the foot of Mount Furnellorum, together with that mountain, as each valley indicates on either side. The allod of Sanzeio, with its own ban, in lands, woods, meadows, waters, and common pastures of the neighbouring villages, which Letardus of Thazeio gave you, with the assent of his wife Alcidis and his heirs John of Morcio, Walter of Vodio, and his son Henry; and Vidricus of Blenau, with the assent of his son Richard and his daughter Bona Filia, and of his heirs John of Moreio, Walter of Vodio and his son Henry, and Matthew, son of Simon of Blenau.

[Col. 1108B] The place of Rengis-Valley with all its appurtenances, which you hold from the chapter of Saint Stephen of Toul, from Havilda of Aspero Monte with the assent of her sons Gobertus and Theodoricus, and from Baldwin of Umplona. The place of Jandoria with all its appurtenances, which you hold from the abbot and chapter of Saint Leo of Toul under a rent of ten solidi to be paid annually. The allod of Utigneio, which Walter of Vodio gave you, with the assent of his brother Simon, his sister Bertha, and his son Matthew; and Hugh Rufus and [Col. 1108C] his brother Henry, with the assent of Hugh’s son and his daughter Hodierna. The little wood called Parvum Porum; ten scythe-measures of meadow in Precra; two scythe-measures of allod between Broceium and Sevodium; and six *journals* of land beside Porum, which Walter of Vadio gave you, with the assent of his son Henry and his daughters Agatha and Aleidis, for his daughters who had entered your church as converts. The eighteen denarii which the same Walter remitted to you in perpetuity, for Havilda his wife, buried in your church. The place of Jovillaris with all its appurtenances, which you hold from Geoffrey of Joinville and Mathilda of Vienne, surnamed Lupa. The place of Gravia in Hungary with all its appurtenances, which you hold from Mendinus, formerly provost of the Church of Alba, with the entire integrity of his patrimony, by assent of all his heirs.

[Col. 1108D] The place of Holy Cross in the March, beside Francavilla, formerly called the Hermitage, with all its appurtenances, lands, meadows, vineyards, and mills. The church of Saint Stephen the King with all its appurtenances. Four scythe-measures of meadow which Hugh, lord of Sorceio, gave you in his enclosed meadow beyond the Nava, for his son Theobald, buried in your church; three scythe-measures of meadow above the ford of Saint Martin, which Garnerus Bocherans, a convert in your church, gave you. Three scythe-measures of meadow in Preca, and two between Sevodium and Wacon, with a vineyard at Bruveium beside the spring called Busita, which Henry of Francavilla gave you [Col. 1109A] for his daughter, who entered your church as a convert. The meadow and vineyard which Otto, knight of Bruleio (Bruley), gave you, with the assent of his wife Thecelina, for his daughter who entered your church as a convert; the vineyards which Oda, wife of Themannus, gave you on Mount Bar, for her daughter who entered your church as a convert; the vineyards which Walter of Vodio, your convert, gave you on the same mountain; the vineyards which Frederick, your convert, gave you behind the monastery; the vineyards which Rainald of Bruleio, your convert, gave you at Risset; the vineyards which Ermengardis of Broceio gave you for her daughter buried in your church; the vineyards which your converts Theodoricus, Wlfardus, Drogo, and Hugh gave you; and the vineyards which Rainaldus Borrei gave you with three *journals* of land at Estrimes, for [Col. 1109B] Hugh his son, a canon in your church. The vineyards, meadows, and lands which Theodoricus, your convert, gave you in the same village. Furthermore, we likewise confirm whatever you hold within the parishes of Brureio, Lucceio, and Langneio, in lands, meadows, vineyards, tithes, and mills.

Indeed, no one shall presume to exact tithes from you on your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the produce of your animals. You may also receive clerics and laymen fleeing from the world, free and absolved, into conversion, and retain them without any opposition.

Moreover, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, to depart from it without the permission of his abbot; and no one shall dare retain one who has departed without letters of authorization from the community. We also forbid churches, lands, or any benefice granted to your church to be given personally to anyone or alienated in any other manner without the consent of your whole chapter or its greater and sounder part; and if any gifts or alienations have been made otherwise than as stated, we deem them void.

[Col. 1109C] To avoid the crowds of secular persons, you may, without prejudice to the right of the diocesan bishop and parish church, build oratories on your granges and, when necessary, celebrate divine offices in them for yourselves and [Col. 1109D] your household.

Furthermore, we decree that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; while preserving, nevertheless, the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. And, desiring with fatherly care to provide for your peace and tranquillity, we prohibit by apostolic authority anyone within the enclosures of your sites or granges from committing violence, robbery, or theft, setting fire, or seizing or killing a person.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, or to take away its [Col. 1110A] possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact, to be of every benefit for the use of those for whose governance or support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical justice of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it, after having been admonished a second or third time, unless he shall make amends for his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the rank of his power and honour, know himself liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and at the last [Col. 1110B] judgment be subject to divine vengeance.

But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theodinus, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina. I, Peter, cardinal priest of Saint Susanna. I, Vivianus, cardinal priest of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Cynthius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. [Col. 1110C] I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement. I, Arduinus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Marcellus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus. I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Ramerius, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Gratianus, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Ranerius, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, [Col. 1110D] on the fourth day before the Kalends of February [29 January], in the fifteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1181, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

### XXXIV. He takes the monastery of Saint Mary of the Wood under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. (Lateran, 30 January.)

[HUGH, *Annals of the Sacred and Canonical Order of Prémontré*, vol. II, Documents, p. CXXXVI.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GUANERUS, abbot of the church of Saint Mary of the Wood, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for perpetual remembrance.

It is fitting that those who choose the religious life should receive apostolic [Col. 1111A] protection, lest an attack of any rashness either draw them back from their purpose or, God forbid, weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of Saint Mary of the Wood, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, decreeing that the canonical order known to have been established in that church according to God, the Rule of blessed Augustine, and the institution of the brethren of Prémontré shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods that church now [Col. 1111B] justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, with the Lord’s help, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their proper terms:

Namely, the valley in which the abbey was founded, from the wood of Saint Glodesindis to the wood of Saint Stephen and to Bellai, together with the hill rising above either side of the aforesaid valley; this Rainaldus and Almaricus, Bertrudis of Venderiis, and Letardus of Villers gave you, with the assent of all their heirs and with the assent of Judith, abbess, and [Col. 1111C] the whole chapter of the nuns of Saint Peter of Metz, and of Simon, duke of Lorraine and advocate of that church. The lower chapel of Saint Mary Magdalene, with its rent, tithes, and all appurtenances. The free chapel of Prismeio, which Matthew, duke of Lorraine, gave you with the assent of Henry, formerly bishop of Toul, and of his sons Simon and Frederick. Part of the allod of Blanzei, which Matthew, duke of Lorraine, gave you, free from every exaction and exempt from every customary due, with the assent of his wife Bertha; his sons Simon, Frederick, Matthew, and Robert, his brother; and Theodoricus of Sassures, advocate of that allod, who surrendered that advocacy into the hand of the duke from whom he held it.

[Col. 1111D] The other part of the same allod, in lands, meadows, vineyards, woods, pastures, and ban, which you hold from Abbot Hugh and the chapter of Saint Aper of Toul under a rent of six solidi in Toul currency, payable annually on the feast of the Holy Innocents. The church of the same village of Blanzei with all its appurtenances—namely its endowment, vineyards, meadows, tithes, offerings, and alms—which you hold from the abbess and chapter of the church of Buxeriis under a rent of six *resalia*, three of rye and three of wheat, payable on the feast of Saint Martin, through the hand of Henry, formerly bishop of Toul, and Hugh Rufus, then archdeacon of that church, who remitted to you in perpetuity the rent belonging to the aforesaid church. The estate of Tautecurt and the estate [Col. 1112A] of Sparnemalla (Sparmalle), which William, advocate of Prisnei, gave you: namely, Tautecurt as he possessed it in length and breadth, from the cross to the ban of Jaunei (Jauny); and the estate of Sparnemalla with all its appurtenances, with the assent of his sons Gerard and Alexander, of all his dependants, and of Matthew, duke of Lorraine, from whom he held the aforesaid estates in fief.

The estate on Mount Parignei, which Drogo of Mancei gave you as he possessed it, from William the advocate’s *croada* [cross], which he delivered to you, to the boundary of Ernaldivilla (Ernaville), and from the forward rock to the wood of Beaunville. The estate of Romermunt with all its appurtenances, which Cono of Asmancia and his son Becelinus, together with his wife Lupa, with the assent of their sons Andrew and Geoffrey, Boemundus of Ramerevilla (Rumereville), their kinsman, and their other coheirs, delivered to you in perpetuity. [Col. 1112B] The allod of Marboge (Marbache), where your grange is situated, which Garsilius of Domeure and his wife Regina gave you with all its appurtenances, with the assent of their son Hugh and daughter Garsilia. The two mill-sites which Fulco of Moreio (Morey) and his countess-wife gave you, with the assent of their son John. The vineyards which you hold at Vanderes, Runamprei, Seuranvigne, and Laureiz, with adjoining meadows in the same village; the vineyards at Villers, with the meadows which you hold in the same village; and the vineyards which you hold [Col. 1112C] at Nouvarai.

Four shares of one-third of the tithes of Parneio (Norroy), both major and minor: one of these you hold from Theodoricus, abbot, and the chapter of Saint Mansnetus of Toul, under a rent of twelve denarii payable annually on the feast of Saint Mansnetus; another from the abbot and chapter of Saint Aggericus of Verdun, under a rent of three *sextarii* of rye; another from Baldwin of Asperomonte, through the hand of the bishop of Toul, with the assent of his sisters Alburgis and Comitissa, his wife Elizabeth, and his sons Simon, Hugh, Formerius, and Albert; and another from Hugh and his brother Reinaldus of Monzuns, through the hand of the aforesaid bishop of Toul.

The vineyard which William, [Col. 1112D] advocate of Prisneio, gave you in the enclosure; the vineyard which Haimo, priest of Prismei, gave you at Franco; the vineyard which Richerus of Warpei gave you; the vineyard which John of Farre gave you at Pronora; the vineyard which John of Rosigno gave you at Vinulis; the vineyard at Vinulis which the brothers Hugh and Gobertus of Vilerces (Villers) gave you; the two vineyards at Vinulis which you hold from your brother Hugh of Prisnei; the vineyard at Prisnei which Walter, priest of the same village, gave you; the vineyard which Hugh, priest of Prisneio, gave you between the castle and the village; the allod in the same place which Ida of Sampigneio gave you, with the assent of her sons Ulricus, Garnerus, and Theodoricus; and the allod in that place which Hauvildis of Parnei gave you [Col. 1113A] with the assent of her daughter, her son Hugh, and Henry of Castro, her husband.

The vineyard in Galterus’ Field which Albert of Parneis gave you; the vineyard which Rechitia gave you in the same place; the vineyard in Daramprei which Suenrus gave you; the vineyard called Rovigne which Letardus of Vilers gave you; the vineyard in the same place which Godefridus and his wife Bonafilia gave you; the vineyard at Fosseis which Widricus, knight of Cusia, gave you; the vineyard at Genval which Letardus of Vilers gave you; the two vineyards at Fosseis which you hold from your brother Gualo; the vineyard near Bellelai which Uscha gave you; three vineyards, two of which you hold in that place and the third at Melaria; the vineyard at Fosseis in the place called Liuns; the vineyard at Murvaldi which [Col. 1113B] Drogo of Claremont gave you; the vineyard in the same place which the brothers Dudardus and Drogo gave you; the vineyard in the same place which Richard gave you; the vineyard beside the winepress which the brothers Drogo and Theobald gave you; the vineyard near the same place, in Hodani-Vineyard, which Drogo gave you; the vineyard in the same place which Garterus Filamont gave you; the vineyard in the same place which Hugh of Claremont gave you; the vineyard in the same place which Drogo and his wife gave you; the vineyard at Melaria which Simon gave you; the vineyard at the spring of Andelandi which Walter, brother of Baldwin, gave you; the vineyard at Bellilei which Lifridus gave you; the vineyard called Bellelai which Ancelinus, knight of Venderia, gave you; [Col. 1113C] the vineyard called Gerundia, which you hold from your sister Rechitia and her daughter Bertrude; the vineyard in the same place which Garinus gave you; two vineyards, one at Blacerio and the other in Alandi-Vineyard, which Aledis of Venderia and her sons Alexander and Simon gave you; the vineyard beside Sorberium which Martinus gave you; the vineyard in Credie-Vineyard which Gista gave you; the vineyard at Gunval which Herbertus gave you; the vineyard in the same place which you hold from your brother Ascelinus Fasne and his wife; the vineyard in the same place which Drogo of Salia and his wife gave you; the vineyard at Winaprei which Rodulphus, son of Aula, gave you; the vineyard in the same place which Holiardis gave you; and the vineyard beside the winepress [Col. 1113D] which the brothers John and Bono of Parneio gave you.

The meadow beside Parneium which Walter and his son Julo, and Richard and Halvindis, gave you. The meadow at Mollum (Moulon) which your sister Rechitia gave you. The five mills which you possess: four of them stand on the river Mantheus—one beside Borleacurt, called Goranges; another beside Vilers, with the meadow in which it stands; and the third and fourth in the ban of Vanderiis—and the fifth lies between Vilers and your abbey. The allod which Witerus of Escrignes gave you within the bounds of your village, in lands, woods, and pastures, with the assent of his wife Ricoldis, his son Garnerus, his sister Heuvildis, and the sons and daughters of that sister, namely Lambertus and Walter, Havuildis and [Col. 1114A] Odilia. The allod in the same bounds, in lands, woods, and pastures, which Hugh of Tireio and his sisters, Hugh of Munzuns and his wife Bonafilia, with the assent of their son Theodoricus and their daughter Falchata, and Hugh of Bricio, with the assent of his sons Herbrannus, Hugh, and Arnulphus, gave you. The allod in the same bounds called Berlairet, which Hauno of Grunsuncurt gave you with the assent of his sons Henry and Stephen; Hugh and Bovo, knights of the same village; and Holiardis, wife of Gerard of Rambertcurt, with the assent of her sons and daughters Fulco, Walter, Hugh, and Elizabeth.

Indeed, no one shall presume to exact tithes from you on your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the produce of your animals. [Col. 1114B] You may also receive clerics and laymen fleeing from the world, free and absolved, into conversion, and retain them without any opposition. Moreover, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, to depart from it without the permission of his abbot; and no one shall dare retain one who has departed without letters of authorization from the community. We also forbid churches, lands, or any benefice granted to your church to be given personally to anyone or alienated in any other manner without the consent of the whole chapter or its greater and sounder part.

If any gifts or alienations have been made otherwise than as stated, we deem them void. [Col. 1114C] Moreover, we add that no canons or converts bound under the protection of your house shall, without the consent and permission of the abbot and the greater part of your chapter, stand surety for anyone or borrow money from anyone beyond the amount provided for by the prudent judgment of their chapter, except for the evident benefit of your house. If anyone presumes to do so, the convent, without whose permission and consent they acted, shall not be bound in any respect to answer for these matters.

Furthermore, you may bring forward suitable brethren to give testimony in your causes and, where just, by their testimony both repel violence and vindicate justice. To avoid the crowds of secular persons, you may, without prejudice to the right of the diocesan bishop and the parish church, [Col. 1114D] build oratories on your granges and, when necessary, celebrate divine offices in them for yourselves and your household. For chrism, holy oil, consecrations of churches, ordinations of clerics to be promoted to sacred orders, the conducting of an abbot to his see, or any other ecclesiastical sacraments, no one shall dare demand anything from you, whether under pretext of custom or in any other manner. If anyone presumes to act against this, let him know that he shall have a portion with Gehazi, whose deed he imitates by exacting a shameful gift. Moreover, we decree that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or [Col. 1115A] under interdict; while preserving, nevertheless, the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken.

And, desiring with fatherly care to provide for your peace and tranquillity, we prohibit by apostolic authority anyone within the enclosures of your sites or granges from committing violence, robbery, or theft, setting fire, or seizing or killing a person.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact, to be of every benefit for the use of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical justice of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theodinus, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Vivianus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Cinthius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement. I, Arduinus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. [Col. 1115C] I, Matthew, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus. I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Rainerius, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Gratianus, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Ranerius, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Kalends of February [30 January], in the fourteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1181, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord [Col. 1115D] Pope Lucius III.

### XXXV. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the Church of Saint Mary of Eugubium. (Lateran.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, I, 639.—The diploma is almost the same as that which Pope Alexander III had already granted them, on the third day before the Kalends of November [30 October] 1170, indiction IV; only the following is distinctive:]

Furthermore, we confirm by this present privilege to you and to that church the liberties and immunities granted from the beginning to you, together with possessions and other goods, by B., bishop of Eugubium of blessed memory; the ancient and reasonable customs of your church; and likewise the tithes, offerings, and mortuary dues which you assert that you have received for forty years and more, just as you possess them lawfully and peacefully. We also prohibit anyone, within the ancient boundaries both of the principal church and of the other churches of your bishopric, from presuming to build anew another parish, church, or oratory without the consent of your bishop and yourselves, while preserving nevertheless the privileges of the Roman pontiffs, etc. If, therefore, in future, etc. This page of our constitution, etc.

Place + of the seal.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theodinus, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Paul, bishop of the Church of Palestrina. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. [Col. 1116B] I, Vivianus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Cinthius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Raynerius, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Gratianus, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Matthew, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on 4 January, in indiction XV, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1181, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

### XXXVI. To I., prior, and the brethren of the church of Saint Frigdianus of Lucca. (Lateran, 2 February.)

[BALUZE, *Miscellanea*, ed. Mansi, IV, 597.]

[Col. 1116C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons I., prior, and the brethren of Saint Frigdianus, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has been reported to us on your behalf that the lord prior of the church of Saint Martin of Siena, without your counsel and assent, son prior, and that of his other brethren, and contrary also to the privileges of the Apostolic See, has in his rashness presumed to impose unprecedented burdens upon that Church. Therefore, since acts committed in an outrageous manner ought to be annulled by apostolic authority, and the fault of an individual must not redound to the injury of the Church, by these present letters we grant you that you shall not be bound in any respect to observe what the aforesaid prior unlawfully did without consulting you, to the manifest detriment of the Church.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Nones of February [2 February].

### XXXVII. He takes the Church of Saint Waldetrudis of Mons under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. (Lateran, 18 February.)

[MIRAEUS, *Diplomatic Works*, III, 350.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in [Col. 1117A] Christ, ELISABETH, prioress of Saint Waldetrudis, and her sisters, present and future, professing the canonical life, in perpetuity.

To the prudent virgins who, under the habit of religion, with lamps kindled through works of holiness, continually prepare themselves to go forth to meet the Bridegroom (Matthew 25), the Apostolic See ought to grant protection, lest an attack of any rashness either draw them back from their purpose or, God forbid, weaken the strength of sacred religion.

Therefore, beloved daughters in Christ, we graciously grant your just petitions, and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the church of Saint Waldetrudis, in which you are devoted to divine service.

[Col. 1117B] First, indeed, decreeing that the canonical order known to have been established in that place according to God and the Rule of blessed Augustine shall be observed there inviolate for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and whatever goods that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the grant of popes, the benefaction of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, acquire through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and to those who succeed you. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: first, the place in which the aforesaid church is situated, with all its appurtenances; whatever you are known to possess near the village of Nimy in lands, meadows, waters, houses, or mills [Col. 1117C]; the altar-right of Comis [Quesne], with its appurtenances, which Lictard, bishop of Cambrai, gave you, and whatever you possess in that village; the altar-right of Framerico, with its appurtenances, given by Albert, formerly bishop of Cambrai, and whatever you possess in that village; the altar-right of Mazca, given by Nicholas, formerly bishop of Cambrai; the altar-right of Castres, with its appurtenances, which Burchard, formerly bishop of Cambrai, gave you, and whatever you are known to possess in that village; the altar-right of Braniavillotica, with its appurtenances, which Lietbert, formerly bishop of Cambrai, gave you, and whatever you are known to possess in that village; the village of Kevy; the village of Kuasrignon; [Col. 1117D] the village of Hal; the village of Herentael; the village of Honestade; the village of Gemapia; male and female serfs assigned to our church; likewise, the rent owed you by the church of Guilenghiem—namely, ten solidi in Valenciennes currency; and the rent owed you by the monastery of Liechies—five solidi in Namur currency.

We decree that the ancient and reasonable customs of your church hitherto observed shall be inviolably observed in perpetuity. Furthermore, no one shall presume to demand or extort tithes from you on your newly cultivated lands, which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals. You may receive for conversion persons fleeing from the secular world who are free and unencumbered, [Col. 1118A] and retain them without any opposition. When a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, you may celebrate the divine offices behind closed doors, without ringing bells, excluding the excommunicated and interdicted, and in a subdued voice.

Moreover, we forbid anyone to pronounce against you or your church a sentence of excommunication, suspension, or interdict without manifest and reasonable cause. We further decree that the burial-ground of that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have decided to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or interdicted; nevertheless, the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken shall be preserved.

[Col. 1118B] We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the complete benefit of the uses for whose governance or support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person [violates this page of our constitution, etc.]

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theodinus, cardinal bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Peter of Tusculum. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina, etc.

[Col. 1118C] Given at the Lateran by the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of March, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1181, and in the first year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Lucius.

### XXXVIII. Takes under protection the convent of St. Mary and St. Peter of Châtel-Carlot, and confirms its possessions and privileges.  
*(Lateran, February 25.)*

[DUNOD, *History of the Sequanois*, vol. I, Documents, p. 100.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, the abbess of the monastery of St. Mary and St. Peter of Châtel-Carlot, and her sisters, present and future, professing the regular life [Col. 1118D] in the aforesaid monastery.

The vigor of equity and the order of reason require that we grant what is justly requested, especially when piety supports the petitioners’ wish and truth does not abandon it. Therefore, beloved daughters in Christ, we graciously assent to your just requests; and, following the example of Urban and Alexander, Roman pontiffs of happy memory, we take the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and our own, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we establish that the monastic order known to have been instituted in the same monastery according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall there be observed inviolably in perpetuity.

Moreover, whatever possessions and whatever goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by grant of popes, benefaction of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, acquire through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and to those who succeed you. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

[Col. 1119A] Noire and half of Ostelens; the church of Moolers with a certain part of its territory; the church of Raons with two holdings in that village; the village of Saint-Lamain with its appurtenances; the church of Brairi; three holdings in the village of Arlay, and the church of St. Vincent; in the castle of Arlay, the chapel of St. Nicholas at Blaterans, sixteen holdings, and half the village of Larnai; at Vincens, five [Col. 1119B] holdings; at Lombar, four holdings; the right which you have in the church of St. German and in the chaplaincy in the village of Playnoisel; the church of St. Remigius and the holding of Moseres; the church of Calmargis; whatever you justly possess in the parish of Vetars; the castle of Galardin, which the nobleman Count William renounced in the presence of you, our beloved daughter in Christ, and of many others; the church of Juvingey; the church of Arinthod; the village of Plesiaci with its appurtenances; the village of Louveres; the village of Moron in [lacuna], three holdings; at Chilim, five holdings; the church of Turbion with the village itself; a third part of Faisse with its church; the church of Fied with the building of Lord Guy the hermit; at Beseno, [Col. 1119C] the church of St. John the Baptist; at Crotenai, the church of St. Peter, the chapel of Novavilla, and the village of Ministroli; the whole of Châtel-Carlot with all its appurtenances; and whatever you possess in the parish of Lons.

Moreover, after William, count of Burgundy and Mâcon, had entered upon the way of all flesh, his wife Countess Pontia, with her sons Stephen and Gerard, in the presence of our venerable brother Humbert, archbishop of Besançon, renounced, out of piety, in favor of the aforesaid church, the tallages and other revenues which they were exacting contrary to justice in its lands. And Tibert of Montmoret, in the presence of certain nobles, relinquished for the remedy and salvation of his soul the church of Paintar, the bell-tower dues and sheaf-dues which he exacted from certain men of the monastery, and the seven denarii which he annually exacted at the feast of St. [Col. 1119D] Martin from each holding and from the church of Châtel-Carlot.

We confirm these same renunciations by the privilege of this present writing, and decree that they shall remain unshaken in perpetuity. Furthermore, desiring to provide hereafter for your peace, by apostolic authority we forbid anyone whatever, without the counsel and assent of you and of those who succeed you, to presume to build towers, houses, or any fortifications upon the possessions of your monastery. We further provide that no one may purchase lands or possessions belonging to your monastery without reasonable cause, and without the knowledge and consent of you or of those [Col. 1120A] who succeed you; and, if anyone purchases them, that sale shall have no validity. In the election of an abbess, moreover, no secular person may presume to claim for himself any voice or power. But upon the death of you, Petronilla, beloved daughter in Christ and abbess, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over that place through any device of fraud or violence, except the one whom the sisters of that place, or the sounder part of the sisters’ counsel, shall, according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict, have determined should be elected.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away, retain, or diminish its possessions, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall remain [Col. 1120B] unimpaired and whole [lacuna] for the complete benefit of the uses for whose governance and instruction they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. Furthermore, as a token of this protection prescribed by the Roman Church, you shall pay ten pounds of wax to the Lateran Palace every seventh year. If in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly, should presume rashly to contravene this page of our constitution, after having been warned a second and a third time, unless he makes fitting satisfaction and corrects his offense, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity perpetrated; let him be alienated from the most sacred body and [Col. 1120C] blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

There follow the signatures of Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, and of many others, both cardinals and bishops; and at the end:

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Kalends of March, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1181, and in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius.  
[Note: [Col. 1119D] The chronological marks are corrupt.]

### XXXIX. Privilege concerning the redemption of tithes for the Church of Osnabrück.  
*(Lateran, March 2.)*

[MOESER, *History of Osnabrück*, IV, 102.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the chapter of St. Peter at Osnabrück, greeting and apostolic blessing.

What is reasonably requested of us ought to be granted by us with willing mind and carried into effect. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, assenting to your just requests, by the authority of these presents we grant you full liberty to redeem, by whatever means you can, the tithes belonging to that church from the hands of laymen, and to apply them to your own uses without any opposition [Col. 1121A] from anyone. Therefore no person may infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly act contrary to it. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Nones of March.

### XL. Privilege concerning tithes not to be granted to a layman.  
*(Lateran, March 3.)*

[IBID., IV, 103.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother [ARNOLD], bishop of Osnabrück, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1121B] Your Fraternity’s prudence does not fail to know, as we firmly believe, that, since tithes cannot be possessed by laymen without peril, they are not to be granted to them under any pretext. Therefore, by apostolic authority we forbid you to assign to any layman tithes which have been taken from lay hands or may hereafter be liberated; rather, you are diligently to devote them to the repair of churches and the support of clerics and the poor, as the canons prescribe, so that through this you may incur neither human reproach nor have cause to fear divine indignation at the supreme judgment.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Nones of March.

LUCIUS POPE III.

### XLI. Privilege concerning burial in the church of Osnabrück.  
*(Lateran, March 3.)*

[IBID.]

[Col. 1121C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, [lacuna] provost and the convent of Osnabrück, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whenever what is requested of us accords with right and does not conflict with ecclesiastical propriety, we ought readily to grant our consent to the petitioners’ desires and carry their vows into effect. Therefore, granting favorable assent to your petitions, we decree that the burial-ground of your church shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who resolve to be buried there, [Col. 1121D] unless they are excommunicated or interdicted; nevertheless, the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken shall be preserved. Therefore no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly act contrary to it. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Nones of March.

### XLII. Confirms the churches and goods of the monastery of St. Cassian of Carisio.  
*(Lateran, March 8.)*

[Annals of Camaldoli, IV, Appendix, p. 107.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1122A] son ANGELO, abbot of St. Cassian of Carisio, and to his brethren, present and future, forever.

Whenever we are asked for something recognized as agreeing with reason and propriety, it befits us to grant it with willing mind and to afford suitable support to the petitioners’ desires.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and take the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and our own, fortifying it by the privilege of this present writing. We establish that whatever possessions and whatever goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grant of popes, benefaction of [Col. 1122B] kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. First, indeed, we establish that the monastic order known to have been instituted in that church according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall there be observed inviolably in perpetuity. We have thought fit to specify the names of the possessions:

The village of Carisio, with its court, jurisdiction, and all its appurtenances, together with the river Rogulo; the church of St. Michael of Monterutrulo, with all that it has and possesses, and with all that you possess in the court and castle of Peczole; [Col. 1122C] the church of St. Cerbonius, with all that you possess in the village and court of Applano; what you possess at Rocoa and in the court of Valli; the share that you possess in the church of St. Justus; everything you possess in the court of Aliga, in the court and jurisdiction of Foliano, on the height of Monte Fusculo, and in the court of Alatreta, together with the church of St. Andrew and everything you possess in that village; the church of St. Pontian, with its height, village, and court; what you possess in the court of Legul, in the court of Toguano, and in the court of the castle of Falfi; the church of St. Peter of Libiano, with what you possess in the village of Libiano; the church of St. Mary of Griciano, with everything that you possess in Griciano and its court; everything you possess at Montecucari, in the court of Monticlo, [Col. 1122D] in the court of Pava, in the court of Casanova, in the village of Padule, in the court of Camuliano, in the court of Palaja, and in the court of Montezano; the church of St. Fridian of Pomponiano, with all its appurtenances, and with everything you possess in the castle, court, and jurisdiction of Bibone; what you possess in the court of Gavorrano; the church of St. Andrew of Ravi, with all that it has and possesses, and everything belonging to you in that same court of Ravi; the church of St. German, with all that it possesses, situated in the court of Collemajori; whatever you possess in the court and jurisdiction of Buriano; and everything you possess in the court of Cumulo and in the court of Ceole.

Furthermore, no one shall presume to demand or extort tithes from you on your newly cultivated lands, which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of [Col. 1123A] your animals. You may also receive into your conversion clerics and laymen fleeing from the secular world, free and unencumbered, and retain them without any opposition.

Moreover, we forbid any of your brethren, after making profession in the same place, to leave that place without his abbot’s permission, except for the purpose of entering a stricter religious order; and no one may dare retain one who has left without letters of authorization from the community. Further, when a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, you may celebrate the divine offices behind closed doors, without ringing bells, excluding the excommunicated and interdicted, and in a suppressed voice. For the parish churches which you hold, you may [Col. 1123B] choose priests and present them to the diocesan bishop; if they are suitable, the bishop shall entrust the care of souls to them, so that they owe accountability to him in spiritual matters and to you in temporal matters. We forbid anyone to pronounce against you a sentence of excommunication or suspension, or against your monastery or churches a sentence of interdict, without manifest and reasonable cause. Moreover, we command that chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of clerics to be promoted to holy orders shall be supplied to you by the diocesan bishop freely and without difficulty.

[Col. 1123C] We further establish that, within the bounds of your parishes, no one may presume to build a new church or oratory without the consent of the diocesan bishop and yourselves, saving, however, the privileges of the Roman Church. Furthermore, we decree that the burial-ground of your monastery shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or interdicted; nevertheless, the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken shall be preserved. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over that place by any device of fraud or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of their counsel, according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict, shall have determined [Col. 1123D] ought to be elected.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away, retain, or diminish its possessions, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the complete benefit of the uses for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person [violates this provision, etc.]

HELP US, O GOD OF OUR SALVATION.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have signed. I, Theodinus, bishop of the see of Porto and Santa Rufina, have signed. [Col. 1124A] I, Peter, bishop of Tusculum, have signed. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina, have signed. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St. Susanna, have signed. I, Vivian, cardinal priest of the title of St. Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have signed. I, Cynthius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Cecilia, have signed. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title of St. Clement, have signed. I, Arduinus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have signed. I, Matthew, cardinal priest of the title of St. Marcellus, have signed. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin, have signed. I, Rainerius, cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, have signed. [Col. 1124B] I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have signed. I, Rainerius, cardinal deacon of St. Adrian, have signed.

[lacuna] by the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Ides of March, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1181, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

(The customary lead seal is appended.)

### XLIII. Privilege for the Church of Modena.  
*(Lateran, March 9.)*

[TIRABOSCHI, *Memoirs of Modena*, III, 82.]

[Col. 1124C] LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BONIFACE, provost of the Church of Modena, and his brethren, present and future, to be canonically appointed in perpetuity.

The vigor of equity and the order of reason require that just petitioners be granted their requests, especially when piety supports the petitioners’ desires and truth does not abandon them. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and, following the example of our predecessor Pope Alexander of happy memory, take the aforesaid Church of Modena, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and our own, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We establish that whatever possessions and whatever [Col. 1124D] goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire through the grant of popes, the benefaction of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, by the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The church of Mocclena; the church of St. Martin of Ponte ducis; the tithe of fish from that place; the holdings of Pelavicinii, Saccuucii, and the count of Massa; the church of Cesa and the holdings which you have there; the church of St. James of Aqualonga and the village of that place; the church of St. Mary of Situla; the castle of Panzani with its court and church; the village of Marzani; the church of St. Maro; the mill [Col. 1125A] and possessions which you have there; half of Castrum Novum and its church; the castle of Petrosa and its church; the village of Prato; the village of Guerlo and its church; whatever you possess in the court of Castrum Vetus; the church of Monte Cuculo; the church of St. Martin of Curso; the parish church of Coligaria with its churches, namely the church of St. Mary in Strata situated beside the river Panaro, the church of St. Dalmatius, and the church of Coligarola; the church of Fossato Regio; the church of Insula; the church of St. Mary Magdalene; the church of St. Cusaldo; and the hospital of that same church; a fourth part of the territory of Miotina, with the tithes belonging to you canonically by right of ownership; the tithes of the fourth part of that same territory belonging to the bishop; the mills canonically situated in the aforesaid fourth part; [Col. 1125B] and whatever you possess at Soleria by exchange made with Manfredino, son of Bernardino, son of the late Manfred.

Furthermore, we hold valid the ancient and reasonable customs of your church hitherto observed, and confirm them by apostolic authority. We also forbid anyone to presume to build a church or oratory within the parishes of your churches without the assent of the diocesan bishop and yourselves, saving, nevertheless, the privileges of the Roman pontiffs. We likewise forbid anyone to presume to pronounce against you or your church a sentence of excommunication or interdict without manifest and reasonable cause. Moreover, we decree that burial in the same church shall be free [Col. 1125C] for the citizens of Modena, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who resolve to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or interdicted; nevertheless, the rights of the parish churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken shall be preserved. Upon the death of you, the present provost of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any device of fraud or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, according to the fear of God, shall have determined is to be elected.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away, retain, or diminish its possessions, [Col. 1125D] or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the complete benefit of the uses for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of your bishop.
