If, therefore, any of the makers of the aforesaid oaths or of that conspiracy, after being warned to abjure them, resist, or should thereafter persist in maintaining or strengthening such assemblies, we grant you free power, by apostolic authority and notwithstanding any opposition or appeal, to excommunicate them. [Col. 1261A–C]

Furthermore, following the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, Alexander and certain other Roman pontiffs, we have thought fit, from the customary clemency and kindness of the Apostolic See, to grant you that if the archbishops or bishops in whose dioceses your wrongdoers are found, having been respectfully, devoutly, and humbly requested by you three times at intervals of three months, fail for a year to render to you and your church full and sufficient justice concerning them, then, after the sounder counsel has been taken and the fitting deliberation observed, you may by our authority bind them with the bond of excommunication during the solemnities of the mass, notwithstanding any appeal or opposition.

With respect to those who have promised fidelity to you and have confirmed by oath that they will abide by the justice of your chapter according to the customs of your church: if, within six months after the archbishops or bishops whose parishioners they are have been requested by you, those prelates have not compelled them to fulfill what they swore to you, as we have said concerning the others, we grant you and confer upon you the same authority and power in every respect. We further add that you may freely declare excommunicated those of your wrongdoers whom archbishops or bishops have excommunicated. [Col. 1261C–1262A]

Furthermore, we prohibit any archbishop, bishop, or other ecclesiastical person from relaxing, without suitable satisfaction, a sentence of excommunication or interdict which you have reasonably pronounced against the aforesaid wrongdoers or your sworn subjects—having observed the form and order stated above and acting with the common counsel, or that of the greater and sounder part. Rather, the sentence itself shall remain valid and firm until worthy amendment, and shall be observed without dispute. Let no person whatsoever therefore infringe this page of our definition, concession, and confirmation, or rashly act against it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul. [Col. 1262A–B]

Given at Veroli, five days before the Kalends of June.

### CXLIX. He grants to Aimeric, prior, and the chapter of Souvigny that “no one shall build a church or chapel within the parishes of that church without their consent, nor pronounce a sentence of excommunication or interdict against the people of Souvigny.” (Castro, 13 June.)

*[Histoire du prieuré de Souvigny, 342, cited by Bréquigny, Table chronologique, IV, 43.]*

### CL. He receives the monastery of St. Mary of Nuovo Porto under protection and confirms its goods and rights. (Ancona, 17 June.)

*[UGHELLI, Italia sacra, I, 332.—The subscriptions of the pope and cardinals, with the date assigned to them, are here presented only; the reader is referred back to the bull granted in the same words by Alexander III to the same monastery. See Patrologia, vol. CC, under Alexander III, for 29 June 1177.]*

[Col. 1262C]

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theodinus, bishop of the see of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Mark. I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of St. Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Callixtus. I, Ardicio, deacon-cardinal of St. Theodore. I, Gratian, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Soffredus, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary in Via Lata. [Col. 1262C–D]

Given at Ancona, through the hand of Hugh, notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of July, in the second indiction, in the year 1183 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

### CLI. He confirms, in favour of the Knights Templar, the donations of Godfrey I, Henry I, and Godfrey II, dukes of Brabant. (Rimini, 22 June.)

*[MIRAEUS, Opera diplomatica, II, 1189.]*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the master and brethren of the house of the knighthood of the Temple: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners and bring to effect the prayers which do not depart from reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, joining your just petitions with favourable assent, we decree valid the pious grant reasonably made to you and your house by Godfrey, once duke of Lorraine, of good memory; and, that it may possess unbreakable force, we have thought fit to insert it in the present letter.

For, divinely inspired, he established that you should henceforth possess and hold profitably for the benefit of your house fifteen *manses*, marshland, and meadows extending to the river Laan, in the place where there had been woodland and which runs beside the land of the monks of St. Mary and the land of the nobleman Gosowin; this was granted by him with the consent of his own wife. [Col. 1263A–B]

Moreover, his grandson Godfrey, duke of Lorraine, with the consent of his own wife, acknowledged and ratified the gift made by his aforesaid grandfather Godfrey; and, following his example, he granted that you should possess the relief-payment of his men both in the duchy of Brabant, in the county of Aarschot, and throughout his land and duchy, as we have learned from his authentic charter.

He further added that whichever of your brethren stays at his court to collect that revenue shall receive from the court, for himself, two squires, and three mounts, hay and oats, candles, and shoeing for the horses. Since all these things were piously and reasonably granted and conceded, we decree that they are valid, confirm them to you and your house by apostolic authority, and strengthen them by the protection of this present writing. We establish that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly act against it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul. [Col. 1263B–C]

Given at Rimini, ten days before the Kalends of July.

### CLII. He forbids the removal of Camaldolese monasteries from the congregation. (Bologna, 7 July.)

*[Annales Camaldulenses, IV, p. 116.]*

[Col. 1263D]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PLACIDUS, prior of Camaldoli, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

The authority of our office admonishes and invites us to labour for the condition of the Churches and, with the Lord’s help, to provide beneficially for their quiet and tranquillity. For it is recognized as worthy and fitting to honour that, since by God’s ordering we have been appointed for their governance, we should both protect them from the wickedness of evil people and fortify them by the protection of blessed Peter and the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and, following the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory—Paschal, Eugenius, Anastasius, Adrian, and Alexander, Roman pontiffs—we command and sanction by the authority of this present decree that no person whatsoever, cleric, monk, or layperson, of whatever order or rank, in present or future times, may in any way separate from its subjection and unity those congregations and places which have adopted the discipline and order of the Camaldolese hermitage or cenobium, and which are today contained under its governance. For the preservation of unity, these places and congregations have seemed fit to be listed individually:

In the diocese of Arezzo: the monastery of St. Saviour of Berardingorum; St. Peter in Rota; St. Mary in Agnano; St. Quiricus in Rosa; the hermitage of Fleri; the monastery of St. Virianus; St. Bartholomew in Anglari; St. Mary of Pratalia; the monastery of Silvaemunda; St. Peter Minor; St. Michael of the Borough; the church at the court of Lupus; St. Andrew of Castellione; St. Sabinus in the territory of Arezzo; and the monastery of St. Mary in Trivio.

In Galiata: the monastery of the Island, New Hermitage, and the monastery of Ferrazzano.

In the diocese of Montefeltro: the monastery of Monte Ercole.

In the diocese of Pesaro: the monastery of St. Dicentius and the hermitage of Sajoli.

In the diocese of Bologna: the monasteries of St. Archangel, St. Felix, St. Christina, and Saints Cosmas and Damian, and the hospital of St. Mary in Ragone.

In the diocese of Faenza: the monastery of St. Hippolytus.

In the diocese of Jesi: the monastery of St. George, the hermitage of Rainald, and the monastery of Accoli.

In the diocese of Camerino: the monastery of St. Helena and the monastery of Pirella.

In the diocese of Spoleto: the monastery of St. Sylvester.

In the diocese of Foligno: the monastery of Landun [lacuna].

In the diocese of Castello: the monastery of the Holy Sepulchre, the monastery of St. Mary of Deciano, and St. Peter of Planeto.

In the diocese of Florence: the monastery of St. Peter in Luco and St. Saviour near the city.

In the diocese of Fiesole: the monastery of Montismuri; the church of St. Margaret; and the monastery of Pratovecchio.

In the diocese of Volterra: the monastery of St. Mary in Policiano, St. Peter in Fontiano, St. Peter in Cerreto, and the monastery of St. Justus.

In the diocese of Pisa: the monastery of St. Mary of Morrona, St. Stephen in Cinctoria, the monastery of St. Sabinus, the monastery of St. Michael of the Borough, St. Fridianus, and St. Zeno.

In the diocese of Lucca: the monastery of St. Saviour in Cantignano and St. Peter in Puteoli.

In Sardinia, in the diocese of Torres: the monastery of the Holy Trinity of Sacraria; the church of St. Eugenia in Samanar; the church of St. Michael and St. Lawrence in Vanari; the church of St. Mary and St. John in Altasar; the church of St. Mary in Contra; the church of St. John and St. Simeon in Salvereno; the church of St. Nicholas of Trulla; the church of St. Peter in Scano; the church of St. Paul in Cotrognano; and the church of St. Peter in Olim.

In Tuscany, in the diocese of Chiusi: the hermitage of Vivo on Mount Amiata, with all the appurtenances of the aforesaid places; moreover, the village of Mojona, which you bought from Henry the provost and the remaining canons, with all its appurtenances; and the village of Montione, which you bought from the abbot of St. Flora, as is contained in your charters and as it was adjudged to you through justice by our predecessor Pope Anastasius of good memory and confirmed by the tenor of his writing. [Col. 1264A–1265A]

We therefore establish and sanction by authority of the Apostolic See that all these monasteries, with all things belonging to them, shall remain for all time, as one body under one head—that is, under the prior of the Camaldolese hermitage—and continue in his observance: namely, under that prior who, with the Lord’s help, shall have been regularly elected by the abbots or priors and the hermits of that congregation. We further decree that the congregation itself shall be fostered forever under the protection of the Apostolic See, so that no bishop may have authority to excommunicate or prohibit any of these monasteries from divine offices without the prior’s consent and permission from the Apostolic See. The brethren themselves may receive the sacraments of consecration and ordination from whichever bishop they prefer. [Col. 1265A–B]

Furthermore, we confirm to you and your convent by apostolic authority the monastery of Urano, without prejudice to the right of the Church of Ravenna. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any other vexations; but that all things shall be kept unimpaired and whole, for the complete benefit of the uses for which they were granted, namely the governance and support of those concerned, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishops. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person shall knowingly attempt in future rashly to act against this page of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amends for the offence by worthy satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and office, acknowledge himself or herself answerable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, and be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of the Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen. [Col. 1265C–D]

**Help us, O God of our salvation.**

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Theodinus, bishop of the see of Porto and Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, have subscribed. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Mark, have subscribed. I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of St. Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Callixtus, have subscribed. I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of the title of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. I, Ardicio, deacon-cardinal of St. Theodore, have subscribed. I, Gratian, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Soffredus, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Albinus, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary the New, have subscribed. [Col. 1266A]

Given at Bologna, through the hand of Hugh, notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of July, in the second indiction, in the year 1183 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III. [Col. 1266B]

### CLIII. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of St. Benignus of Dijon. (Verona, 31 July.)

*[PÉRARD, Recueil, 258.]*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HAMON, abbot of St. Benignus of Dijon, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

To grant effect to just requests is demanded by the force of equity and the order of reason, especially when piety supports the will of the petitioners and truth does not abandon it. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and, following the example of our predecessors of blessed memory, Roman pontiffs Gregory VII, Honorius, Innocent, and Alexander, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid monastery in which you are devoted to the divine service. First, we decree that the monastic order known to have been established in that place according to God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, with the Lord’s help, acquire by grant of pontiffs, gift of kings or princes, offering of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: [Col. 1266C–D]

… are situated in your …, the freedom of the priests … of the churches serving the Lord, which Robert, formerly bishop of Langres, granted to the monastery … and which our brother Manasses, bishop of Langres, likewise granted to you in the same … churches of Saint Apollinaris and of Longo Vado, of Plombières and of Villars, in perpetuity, and confirmed by his own document; the church of Saint Germanus of Lariacum, in which nuns reside—on the condition that the nuns themselves render to you, to your successors, and to the church of Dijon the due and customary obedience, as the monks of the same place are known to render it—we nevertheless confirm to you, as you possess it canonically and peacefully; also the cell of Clement’s Meadow, in which lay brothers reside; the place of Fordemunt, in which lay brothers likewise reside; and that remission and immunity which Robert, formerly bishop of Langres, of good memory, or his predecessors, are known reasonably to have granted you concerning *paratae* and synods: we confirm it by the authority of the present writing. Moreover, we likewise confirm by apostolic authority, with all its appurtenances, the estate called Dianetum, as it was justly adjudged to your monastery by the judgment of Stephen, bishop of Autun, and as you possess it peacefully. [Col. 1267A–B]

Furthermore, no one shall presume to demand or extort tithes from you on your newly cultivated lands, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the produce of your animals. You may also receive into your conversion clerics or laymen fleeing the world, free and unbound, and retain them in your monastery without any opposition. Moreover, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, from leaving without the permission of the abbot or his official, except for the sake of a stricter religious life; and no one may dare retain one who leaves without letters of authorization from the community. Whenever a general interdict is imposed upon the land, you may celebrate the divine offices behind closed doors, excluding the excommunicated and interdicted, without ringing bells and in a low voice. [Col. 1267B–C]

In the parish churches which you possess, you may nominate priests and present them to the diocesan bishop. If they are suitable, the bishop shall entrust them with the care of souls; they must answer to him in spiritual matters and to you in temporal matters. We also decree that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last wishes of those who have determined to be buried there, saving nevertheless the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. And those things which our predecessors Sergius, John, and Alexander, by prudent deliberation, granted you concerning the cemetery or other matters, as contained in their privileges, we decree shall henceforth remain unimpaired. [Col. 1267C–D]

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, or take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole and unimpaired, wholly benefiting the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
[Col. 1268A] I, Theodinus, bishop of the see of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus. I, Humbert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. I, Pant[ulf], cardinal priest of the title of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Arditio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. [Col. 1268B] I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Joffredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Albinus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Hugh, notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of August [31 July], in the second indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1184, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

## CLIV. He receives the Church of Saint Peter of Nessina under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges.  
*(Verona, 10 August.)*

[TATTI, *Annals of Como*, vol. II, p. 884.]

[Col. 1268C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the provost of the church of Saint Peter of Nessii and his brethren, both present and future, to be canonically appointed, forever.

Whenever that is requested of us which appears consonant with reason and propriety, it befits us gladly to grant it and to bestow fitting support upon the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of Saint Peter, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the protection of the present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have judged it proper to specify the following in their own terms:

The very place in which the said church is situated, with all the adjacent property belonging to it. From the gift and grant of B., bishop of Como, a fourth part of the tithe of your said parish. The clearing of Saint John of Domo, which Stephen the archpriest cultivated. The island wood which the said bishop had bought. The oratories of Saints Victor and Nazarius of Brienno, with all their appurtenances. The tithe from the house of Crescentius of Brienno. The oratory of Saints George and Nazarius of Hillo, with all its appurtenances. The oratory of Saint Andrew the Apostle of Nervo, with all its appurtenances. The oratory of Saint Mary of Vico, with all its appurtenances. The oratory of Saint Martin of Careno, with all its appurtenances. The oratory of Saint Mary and Saint Fidelis of Ciserno, with all its appurtenances. The oratory of Saint Ambrose of Palanzo, with all its appurtenances. The oratories of Saint Mary and Saint Alexander of Hemena, with all their appurtenances. [Col. 1269A] The oratory of Saint Margaret of Molina, with all its appurtenances; the land of Curticella; the tithe from the house of Urso of Pino and of John the priest, his brother; the tithe from the house of Peter the priest and his nephews; the tithe from the house of the sons of Stephen the priest; the tithe of the sons of Martin of Calcariola; and the benefice of custody. [Col. 1269B]

We therefore decree that no one whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved unimpaired and whole, wholly benefiting the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our protection, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless he correct his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject to divine vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen. [Col. 1269B–C]

Given at Verona, through the hand of Hugh, notary, on the fourth day before the Ides of August [10 August], in the second indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1184, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

## CLV. He confirms the convent of the Holy Saviour and Saint Julia at Brescia, with its goods, rights, and jurisdictions, under the protection of the Holy Roman Church.  
*(Verona, 18 August.)*

[MARGARINI, *Casinensian Bullary*, II, 205.]

[Col. 1269D]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, GRACE, abbess of the monastery of Saint Julia at Brescia, and her sisters, both present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

The Apostolic See ought to grant protection to prudent virgins who, under the habit of religion, with lamps kindled, continually prepare themselves through works of holiness to go out to meet the Bridegroom, lest perhaps an assault of any rashness recall them from their purpose or, God forbid, weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved daughters in Christ, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the guardianship of blessed Peter and our protection the aforesaid monastery of Saint Julia at Brescia, in which you are devoted to divine service, which is known to belong directly, without intermediary, to the right and property of blessed Peter. Following the example of our predecessors of happy memory, Calixtus, Innocent, and Eugenius, Roman pontiffs, we strengthen it by the privilege of the present writing. We decree that whatever estates, possessions, and goods the monastery now justly and canonically possesses—from the munificence of Queen Ansa of good memory, from the generosity of the emperors of illustrious memory who assumed the government of the realm after her, or from gifts of other faithful persons—or may hereafter acquire, by the grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and to those who succeed you. Among these we have judged it proper to specify the following in their own terms:

Sermione, with the two churches of our Lord the Saviour and Saint Vitus the martyr; Cervanica, with the church of Saint Julia the martyr; Nubelaria, with the church of Saint Lawrence; Berciago, with the two churches of Saint Zeno and Saint Stephen; Magonenvicum, with the church of Saint Alexander; Thimolina, with the church of Saint Julia; Barbada, [Col. 1270C] with the two churches of Saint Mary and Saint Julia, and Saint Peter; Monticello, with the church of Saint Mary; Voum, with the churches of Saint Peter and Saint Lawrence; Calvatone, with the churches of Saint Mary, Saint Julia, and Saint Blaise; Scandolaria, with the church of Saint Michael; Cicomaria, with the church of Saint Mary; Gosenago, with the church of Saint Martin; Miliarina, with the church of Saint Julia; Sermida, with the church of Saint Peter in Solado, and the chapel of Saint Julia of Pradellis. Moreover, we likewise confirm all other *curtes*, estates, castles, churches, the port of Piacenza and its river-dues, the jurisdiction over slaves and free persons belonging to your convent, and everything belonging to the same monastery. [Col. 1270C–D]

Furthermore, no one shall presume to demand or extort from you tithes on your newly cultivated lands which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the produce of your animals. We also confirm to you, and through you to the same monastery, by apostolic authority, the tithes which the monastery has possessed without challenge for forty years and now possesses without dispute. By the present decree we further establish that the aforesaid monastery, fortified by the protection of the Apostolic See and royal defence, shall never be made subject to the power or jurisdiction of any other person; so that no priest may presume to celebrate there the solemn rites of Mass unless invited by the abbess of that place.

Moreover, we grant the abbess of that place permission to build churches for the honour of God; and we likewise confirm the freedom granted to the aforesaid monastery by emperors and kings, both in establishing markets and in constructing castles on the lands of that monastery, wherever she wishes for the monastery’s benefit. No bishop, duke, marquis, count, viscount, or any great or small person shall presume to exercise or judge any jurisdiction in any place belonging to the monastery, hold any court without the abbess’s permission, alienate in any manner its spiritual or temporal property, inflict injury upon it, or dare to demand *fodrum* [a royal due], lodging-duty, river-dues, *paratae*, or any services whatsoever. [Col. 1271A]

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, the ordination of the abbess or nuns, or of your clerics who are to be promoted to holy orders, and whatever pertains to sacred ministry, from whichever Catholic bishops you prefer, provided that they grant these to you without any perversity or reproach, as it is evident was granted to your monastery by our aforesaid predecessors Calixtus, Innocent, and Eugenius, Roman pontiffs, because of the weakness of the female sex. When you, the present abbess of that place, or any one of those who succeed you dies, no person shall be appointed there by any deceitful device or violence, except one whom the sisters by common consent, or the sounder part of the sisters’ counsel, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict. [Col. 1271B–C]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole, wholly benefiting the uses of those for whose governance they were granted. We establish all the foregoing by the authority of the Roman Church. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless he correct his offence by worthy satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen. [Col. 1271C–D]

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, Theodinus, bishop of the see of Porto and Santa Rufina. [Col. 1272A] I, John, cardinal priest of the title of the church of Saint Mark. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mary across the Tiber. I, Pandulphus, cardinal priest of the title of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Theodore. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of the title of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Goffredus, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Albinus, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Mary the New.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Hugh, notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of September [18 August], in the second indiction, [Col. 1272B] in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1184, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

The sign of Pope Lucius III.

**HELP US, O GOD, OUR SAVIOUR.**

## CLVI. Papal bull for the monastery of Bon-Radi.  
*(Verona, 31 August.)*

[*Gallia Christiana nova*, XII, Instrument 138.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, GIRARD, abbot of the monastery of Bon-Radi, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

It is fitting that apostolic protection be present for those choosing the religious life, lest perhaps an assault of any rashness recall them from their purpose or, God forbid, weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery of Bon-Radi, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of the present writing. First, we decree that the monastic order established in your convent according to the fear of God, the Rule of blessed Benedict, and the institution of the Cistercian brethren shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God propitious, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have judged it proper to specify the following in their own terms:

The place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with all its appurtenances, extending from the beaten road leading from Nevers to Varzy as far as the old road leading from La Charité to Varzy; and all rights of common use throughout the entire lordship of Candemisius, both in woods and on open ground: the wood called Booles; the grange of Bon-Radi with its appurtenances; pastures in Boiplain; the grange of Cathelai with its appurtenances; the lands of Lambert Salons; Milo’s wood; the wood called Castales (*Chastelet*); the lands of Gaudricus; the road by which one goes [Col. 1273A] to the grange; the grange of Caviniac (*Chevigny*) with its appurtenances; the grange of the aqueduct with its appurtenances; the wood given you by the lady of Grenat; rights of common use in the wood of Britan [lacuna]; the grange of Avantages with its appurtenances; the small fief; likewise the open wood called Noardes; the mill of Pruvera and the millstone of those mills; the land called Caumes (*Chaumes*), given to you by Everard Motet; the grange of Concis with its appurtenances; the meadows and lands of Lady Mary of Nauminia (*Naumain*); the Red Forest; the house and vineyards of Varzy; the house and vineyards of Serbent; Mont-Agleuti (*Montaiglaut*) and its vineyards; Pont-tilium; the lands of Constablei (*Constables*); Galeraud’s meadow (*Pré Galeraud*) and the water-control structure of that meadow; Noassegaudi (*Novesegaud*); the Meadows of the Angels (*Pré des Anges*) as far as the quarry; the meadows of Saint Macuti; the meadow of Peter Constables; and the meadows of Linerolas (*Ligneroles*). [Col. 1273A–B]

Furthermore, no one shall presume to demand or extort tithes from you on your cultivated lands, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the produce of your animals. You may also receive clerics or laymen fleeing the world, free and unbound, into your conversion and retain them without any opposition. Moreover, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, from leaving it without the permission of his abbot; and no one may dare retain one who leaves without letters of authorization from the community. Desiring, moreover, by paternal concern to provide for your peace and tranquillity, we prohibit by apostolic authority anyone within the enclosures of your places or granges from presuming rashly to commit violence, robbery, or theft, set fire, seize, or kill a person. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, etc. [Col. 1273B–C]

Given at Verona, through the hand of Hugh, notary of the most holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of September [31 August], in the second indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1184, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

## CLVII. He receives the Upper Altaich Monastery under protection and confirms its goods and rights.  
*(Verona, 2 September.)*

[*Monumenta Boica*, vol. XII, p. 112.]

[Col. 1273D]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WOLFRAN, abbot of the monastery of Saint Peter in Alta, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

Whenever that is requested of us which is recognized as consonant with religion and propriety, it befits us gladly to grant it and to bestow fitting support upon the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery of Saint Peter in Alta, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of the present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have judged it proper to specify the following in their own terms:

The place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with all its appurtenances: Drasselesriede, Ossenpach, Leivannesriede, Calberespach, Haimesperge, Aitinha, Plassanesperch, Adelhartesdorf, Hagenperg, Heich, Melpach; three holdings at Pirche; Gocholdesgrube; Chroleinesdorf; Hubenare; three holdings at Borascelle; three holdings at Toveranesdorf; Renften; two holdings; Sikeleinesperge; Mennaha. A mill; Hicenperge; an estate; Grube; one estate. Ricemannesdorf, three holdings; Temanesdorf, three vineyards and whatever you possess there. Velberch, one holding; Teusenbach, two holdings next to one holding. Mertanne, Puchperge, Radesmannesperge, Menna, one holding and a mill. Haugencelle; Freindorf; the holding of Riute; two holdings. Harde; Strazchirchen; Vulpach, one *mansus* [holding]. At Buizchouen, two holdings; Maetingen, one holding. Silichinge, three holdings; Haiterhouen, nine *mansi*; Wintpozzingen, one holding. Harde; Hunderdorf, three holdings; Scorringe, half a *mansus*; Berndorf, three [Col. 1274C] *mansi*. Dietrichesdorf, one holding; Tatingem, one *mansus*; Hovedorf, two holdings. Pinningen, one holding; Mirendorf, an estate; Wacenriede, an estate; and Laderaren, four holdings.

Furthermore, no one shall presume to demand or extort tithes from you on your newly cultivated lands, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the produce of your animals.

You may also receive into your conversion clerics or laymen fleeing the world, free and unbound, and retain them without any opposition. Moreover, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, from leaving that place without the permission of his abbot, except for the sake of a stricter religious life; and no one may dare retain one who leaves without letters of authorization from the community. Moreover, we confirm to you the tithes which you have held without challenge for forty years. Whenever a general interdict is imposed upon the land, you may celebrate the divine offices behind closed doors, excluding the excommunicated and interdicted, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice. In the parish churches which you possess, you may elect priests and present them to the diocesan bishop. If they are suitable, the bishop shall entrust them with the care of souls, so that they must answer to him in spiritual matters and to you in temporal matters. [Col. 1274C–D]

We also prohibit by apostolic authority your advocate, whoever he may be at the time, from presuming on any pretext to exercise violence in your monastery or alienate its goods; rather, let him be content with the right which is known to have been established for him of old. But if he appears burdensome to the brethren and useless to the monastery, we grant to you and your successors, by apostolic authority, the power, once he has been removed, to elect another suitable advocate. We further decree that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last wishes of those who have determined to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or interdicted, saving nevertheless the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. When you, the present abbot of that place, or any of your successors dies, no person shall be appointed there by any deceitful device or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict. [Col. 1275A–B]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole, wholly benefiting the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1275C] I, Theodore, bishop of the see of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus. I, Pandulfus, cardinal priest of the title of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, Arditio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gofredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Albinus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New.

[Col. 1275D] Given at Verona through the hand of Hugh, notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Nones of September [2 September], in the second indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1184, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

## CLVIII. Privilege concerning the use of the mitre for the abbots of Saint Michael of Bamberg.  
*(Verona, 4 September.)*

[USSERMANN, *Episcopate of Bamberg*, Proofs, p. 126.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son WOLFRAN, abbot of Saint Michael on Mount Bamberg, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Those who show pure and sincere devotion to the most holy Roman Church we regard, as is fitting, with more gracious kindness; and we do not deny the assent of our favourable disposition to their just requests. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, assenting to your just petitions and favourably carrying out the requests of our venerable brother O., bishop of Bamberg, we grant to your successors also the use of the mitre which has been granted personally to you, so that your church may always have the mitre before its eyes, in which it may recognize the more abundant favour and grace of the Apostolic See shown to it. Let no one, therefore, etc. [Col. 1276A]

Given at Verona, on the second day before the Nones of September [4 September].

## CLIX. He attests that he consecrated the churches of Bologna and Modena, without prejudice to the right of Gerard, archbishop of Ravenna.  
*(Verona, 4 September.)*

[RUBEUS, *History of Ravenna*, p. 356.]

[Col. 1276B]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GERARD, archbishop of Ravenna, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting and consonant with reason that, since at the request of your brotherhood we have bestowed the gift of consecration upon the churches of Bologna and Modena, they should never be able on this account to claim any degree of freedom against your church, to which they are subject as to their metropolitan. Therefore, wishing to provide that no ground for injury or scandal may arise from our action to you or your successors, we establish by apostolic authority that no prejudice shall in future result from this to you or your successors, but that the aforesaid churches shall always remain, as they were before the consecration which we bestowed upon them, without opposition in the obedience and subjection of you and your successors. No person whatsoever may infringe this page of our constitution or rashly oppose it. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. [Col. 1276B–C]

Given at Verona, on the second day before the Nones of September [4 September].

## CLX. Privilege for the Church of Saint Thomas of Reggio.  
*(Verona, 9 September.)*

[TIRABOSCHI, *Memoirs of Modena*, III, 94.]

[Col. 1276D]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, BEATRICE, abbess of Saint Thomas of Reggio, and her sisters, both present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

The Apostolic See ought to grant protection to prudent virgins who, under the habit of religion, with lamps kindled, continually prepare themselves through works of holiness to go out to meet the Bridegroom, lest perhaps an assault of any rashness recall them from their purpose or, God forbid, weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved daughters in Christ, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of Saint Thomas, in which you are devoted to God’s service, and strengthen it by the privilege of the present writing. First, we decree that the monastic order which is known to have been instituted in that place according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have judged it proper to specify the following in their own terms:

The place itself in which the said church is situated, as the royal highway comes to the road of Holy Cross, and from that road runs to the city ditch; and within, as the ditch extends as far as the holding of the sons of Balbus, and from that place returns to the royal highway; the parish church of Mutilena, dedicated in honour of Saint Michael, with its chapels and appurtenances—namely, the chapel of Saint Mary of Sisio, with all belonging to the same church; the chapel of Saint Dalmatius, with its appurtenances; the chapel of Saint Celestine, with its appurtenances, at Vicojoario; the chapel of Saint Blaise at Runcocesso, with all its appurtenances; the rights which you possess in the church of Curviaco; the chapel of Saint Paul in the city, with all belonging to the same church; the church of Saint Vitus, with all belonging to the same church; the church of Saint Vigilius [Col. 1277C] at Saxo-Forte, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Blaise of Villanova, with its appurtenances; the church of the Holy Lord at Fozano, with all its appurtenances; the land held from your church by Asto of Novis, under the name of Libellarius, with houses, building-plots, and vineyards; thirteen *iugera* of land and a building-plot in the city—all of which Lady Beatrice held from your church under a precarious grant—and the *mansus* of Monte held by Guido and his nephew, as you possess these things justly and without dispute. Furthermore, no one shall presume to extort from you tithes on your newly cultivated lands, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the produce of your animals. [Col. 1277A–C]

Since the proceeds of tithes are assigned to churches and their persons, we prohibit any layman from demanding tithes from your lands or revenues. Moreover, we forbid any archbishop to pronounce against you or your church a sentence of suspension or excommunication without manifest and reasonable cause. You may also … receive persons fleeing the world, free and unbound, into your conversion and retain them without any opposition. Whenever a general interdict is imposed upon the land, you may celebrate the divine offices without ringing bells, behind closed doors, excluding the excommunicated and interdicted, in a subdued voice. We further decree that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last wishes of those who have determined to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or interdicted, saving nevertheless the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. [Col. 1277D–1278A]

We will that the ancient and reasonable customs of your church, preserved unchallenged and without dispute until the present time for forty years, shall remain unimpaired by apostolic authority. When you, the present abbess of that place, or any of those who succeed you dies, no person shall be appointed there by any deceitful device or violence, except one whom the sisters by common consent, or the sounder part of the sisters’ counsel, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict.

We therefore decree that no one whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole, wholly benefiting the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. [Col. 1278B]

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, etc.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theodinus, bishop of the see of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. [Col. 1278C] I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Soffredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. [Col. 1278D] I, Albinus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Hugh, notary, on the fifth Ides of September [9 September], in the third indiction, in the year 1184 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

## CLXI. Privilege for the Church of Saint Evasius of Casale.  
*(Verona, 24 September.)*

[CONTI, *Historical Memoirs of Casale*, I, 357.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons STEPHEN, provost of the church of Saint Evasius of Casale, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

A petition of pious desire ought to be fulfilled by its resulting effect [Col. 1279A] etc. [lacuna], and, following the example of our predecessors of blessed memory, Calixtus, Paschal, and Innocent, Roman pontiffs, we fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree first of all that the canonical order known to have been established in this church according to God and the Rule of blessed Augustine shall be preserved there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions or goods your church now justly and canonically holds, or may hereafter acquire, with the Lord’s aid, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

All churches situated within the precinct of Casale, with all their appurtenances; the church of Saint Hilary and the house of ecclesiastical labour; at Paciliano, the church of Saint Germanus, etc.; the holding of Radulf Quecea, with first-fruits and a third part of the tithes of the whole place of Casale; the whole tithe from the lands of the household of Saint Evasius; the whole tithe of Bishop Brayda; and whatever the church of Paciliano has customarily rendered to your church by right or long custom; the village of Luvintini with its tithes and all appurtenances. At Saint George, fourteen holdings; a sixteenth part of Torcello and the former holding of Peter Crassus, with all their appurtenances. At Montedo, three holdings. At Fraxinetum, one and a half holdings. [Col. 1279C]

Certainly, no one shall presume to take tithes from you of newly cleared lands which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the produce of your animals. You may also receive into your religious conversion clerics or laymen of the city fleeing the world, provided that they are free and absolved, and retain them in your church without any opposition. We further forbid any of your brethren, after making profession in your house, to leave the cloister without the permission of his provost; and no one shall dare retain a departing brother unless he bears a joint letter of authorization. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of clerics to be advanced to sacred orders from the diocesan bishop, provided [Col. 1279D] that he is Catholic, enjoys the grace and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to confer these upon you freely and without any improper exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer; supported by our authority, he shall grant what is requested.

Upon the death of you, the present provost of this place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any stratagem of deceit or violence, save the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall provide to be chosen according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Augustine.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, [Col. 1280A] retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass them by any vexations; but all things shall be preserved whole for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Hubert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Theodorus, bishop of the see of Porto and Santa Rufina. [Col. 1280B] I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Goffredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Albinus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Hugh, notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of October [24 September], in the third indiction, in the year 1184 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

## CLXII. He takes the monastery of Saint Peter of Radolium under protection and confirms its goods.  
*(Verona, 26 September.)*

[*Bullarium Cluniacense*, 79.]

[Col. 1280C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons SIMON, prior of the monastery of Saint Peter of Radolium, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Whenever you ask for something known to accord with religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and afford suitable support to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery of Saint Peter of Radolium, [Col. 1280D] which is known to belong to the monastery of Cluny and in which you are dedicated to divine service; and we fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions or goods the same monastery now justly and canonically holds, or may hereafter acquire, with the Lord’s aid, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, together with the whole village of Radolium and its appurtenances; and everything which you possess near the boundaries of that [Col. 1281A] village, in woodland as well as on the plain; the church of Saint Stephen of Condeiacum, with its tithes and two portions of the *tortelli* on the day after the Nativity of the Lord, and of candles at the Purification of Blessed Mary; the chapel of Saint Martin in the same parish; nine arpents of meadow between the same place and the bridge of Conde; the oven and mill of the stronghold of Anculfus; the church of Chaminiacum with tithes and the chapel of Blessed Mary Magdalene situated in the same place; a third part of the tithes of Lusenciacum, with the other tithes and revenues which you hold in the same parish; one mill at Vavas, with the meadow called Brubium, as well as tenants, and the other revenues and meadows which you possess in the parishes of Chaminiacum and Lusentiacum; the lands, waters, meadows, woods, and [Col. 1281B] tenants which you possess at Grupellariae and Canescellum; and, at Caminiacum, eight sextaries of oats, which Ausculfus of Marvo renders for the exchange of a mill; the church of Chaelliacum, with tithes and offerings, and whatever you possess in that parish, in lands, land-rents, or other revenues; the church of Bussy, with tithes, two portions of candles at the Purification of Saint Mary, and two portions of offerings at Easter, the Nativity of the Lord, and the feasts of All Saints and Saint Sulpicius; the church of Duciis, with a third portion of *tortelli* at the Nativity of the Lord and of candles at the Purification of Saint Mary; the land of Chalmot; the wood of Rugel; the wood of Bulard, together with the wood of Molera in the parish of Staalda; a half-share in a mill; the tithes and other revenues, lands, [Col. 1281C] tenants, and meadows which you hold at Teviants; a tenth part of the tithe of Montiniacum on that side of the water which faces the church, excepting the waters and calves; the land and meadows of Usco; a third part of the tithe of Mesilam in grain, with the related levy, and a third part of the small tithes; at Iahamias, arable land with twenty-three denarii of quit-rent; six solidi of quit-rent in the church of Venderia; and eleven portions of the tithes, both small and other tithes, and of the *tortellae* at the Nativity of the Lord, and all candles at the Purification of Blessed Mary, excepting twelve [candles] and excepting the small tithes of four tenants of Saint Faron; the lands, meadows, persons or tenants, and revenues which you possess in that parish. [Col. 1281D]

A third part of the tithes of Huguerre, with a third part of the *tortelli* at the Nativity of the Lord; the lands, tenants, and other revenues which you possess at Loriacum; half the tithe of Crespeel, with the related levy, at Vendeul; a third part of the tithe of Saint Julian, with a third part of the tenants, churchyard, and *tortellae*, and what you possess in tithes and revenues at Gandelus; half a modius of wheat from the mill of Trema; the chapel of Blessed Mary of Lisiacum, with three modii of wheat received at the mills of that place, and ten solidi, together with two modii of wine and two denarii each week in the market, and all other things belonging to the same chapel in that place and at Villeriae; half the grain tithe with the related levy, and one [Col. 1282A] additional septary in every modius; the money which you possess at Asveriae; at Eschancru, four solidi of quit-rent; from the land of Salviniacum, in the church of Placeium, a fourth part of the *tortelli* and offerings at the Nativity of the Lord, Easter, the feast of All Saints, and Saint Victor’s feast, and two portions of the tithes; the village called Bennarim, with its appurtenances and jurisdiction; and everything that you possess in persons, meadows, and quit-rents at Congiacum and Uvivum; a sixth part of the grain tithe; at Sanctipelliacum, two sextaries of oats and two of wheat, with land-rent and quit-rent; at Orthollim, two portions of the tithe; four sextaries of wheat, to be received at the grange of Saint Faron; at Vanderia, in exchange for Panchat.

In the city [Col. 1282B] of Meaux, the church of Saint Christopher, with a third part of offerings at the Nativity, Epiphany, Easter, Pentecost, the feast of All Saints, and, at the Purification of Blessed Mary and the feast of Saint Christopher, a third part of the candles. Likewise in the same city, a third part of the quit-rents which they have by the gift of Wiard of Venderia, together with certain quit-rents; half a modius of grain which the lepers of that city render to you; for the land of Chamolt, two portions of the tithe of Varenna, with the right of presentation, which you possess in those churches; and, in your villages and over your people, free jurisdiction, as confirmed by an authentic written instrument from Countess Ada and her son Hugh. Likewise, the tithe of Firmitas and Canday, in wine as well as grain; the village of Eleemosynarius; the villarium with jurisdiction; the village of Vorpellariae with jurisdiction, given by Agatha; the tithe of Chaviniacum; half the tithe of Nucimentum; the mill of Vannis; the wood and tenants of Chasverel, given by Radulf of Montmirail; the allod of Chamot with its appurtenances; [Col. 1282C] also the men and maidservants of Firmitas, as Hugh the White had held them; the allod of Pavant, with eight tenants, their jurisdiction, and their possessions; the tithe of Rutel; the allod of Crutis, given by William Joharannus; the land and revenue of Freneco, given by Peter of Trema and his brother Simon; the land and tenants of Jorcham, given by Reginald Gurdon.

Likewise, the land, tithe, quit-rent, and house of Anculfus of Conde; at Lori and Tauro, half the land and the grange of Duciis, given by Robert of Lisy; the land of Cusiis, given by Robert of Lisiaro, Goonis, Gaudi, and Odo of Staalda; the tithe of Montiniacum; the oven of Gaudeluc and the oven-due of the same castle, granted by the aforesaid countess and her son Hugh; the use of the oven and house, as is contained in their authentic written instrument; in the church of Blessed Mary of Duciis, five modii of wheat in the granary of Meaux; twenty solidi from the customary due called *passagium*; two sextaries of salt every year; the right and house situated beside the house, given by the aforesaid viscountess and her son; also the dead-hand dues and recognitions from male and female serfs which Hugh the White gave, at the strongholds of Anculfus. [Col. 1283A]

As he himself held them: the chapel of Saint Mary of Fonte Sereno with its appurtenances; and whatever you possess at Naudelu, Choisy, and Cury; ten solidi from Bernard of Charon; [materially uncertain: “quos sextarios frumenti apud Choisy”]; four sextaries of grain at Choisy; in the tithe of Canos, whatever you possess at Latingis; at Currem, the church of that place with the presentation of its priest; whatever you possess at Frenios, Trebure, Curtogiis, Château-Thierry, Varenas, Panant, Crutis, Neustorel, Cardulet, Villarium, Vestulum, Vuelli, and Selonts; half of the great mill; and whatever you possess at Buzae, Bivul, and Premant; half the tithe of Damant; and whatever you possess at Lory, Socom, and Villerslevast; whatever you possess in the stronghold of Anculfus and its boundaries, given by the aforesaid viscountess Ada and her son Hugh, as is contained in their authentic written instrument. We likewise confirm to you all other possessions which your monastery has held without disturbance for forty years and which you now possess without controversy.

Certainly, no one shall presume to demand or exact tithes from you of newly cleared lands which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the produce of your animals. You may receive into your religious conversion clerics or laymen fleeing the world, provided that they are free and absolved, and they may remain without any opposition. We further prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in the same place, [Col. 1283C] from leaving that place without the permission of his prior, except on account of a stricter religious observance; and no one shall dare canonically receive a departing brother without the testimony of joint letters. When a general interdict has been laid upon the land, you may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, excluding excommunicated and interdicted persons, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice. We also prohibit anyone from presuming to build a church or oratory within the boundaries of your parishes without the consent of the diocesan bishop and yourselves, without prejudice, however, to the privileges of Roman pontiffs.

Moreover, we hold ratified your ancient liberties and immunities, and the reasonable customs granted to your monastery and hitherto observed; and we decree that they shall remain unimpaired in future times. We decree that the burial-place of that house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who choose to be buried there, unless they are perhaps excommunicated or interdicted, without prejudice, however, to the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. [Col. 1283D]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass them by any vexations; but all things shall be preserved whole for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See, the right of the diocesan bishop, and the due reverence owed to the monastery of Cluny. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Hugh, notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Kalends of October [26 September], in the third indiction, in the year 1184 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

## CLXIII. Privilege for the Church of Treviso.  
*(Verona, 1 October.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 530.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother CONRAD, bishop of Treviso, and to his successors canonically appointed: in perpetuity.

[Col. 1284B] Set upon the lofty watchtower of the Apostolic See, we ought to love our brother bishops, both near and far, with brotherly charity, and to provide with paternal care for the churches over which, by God’s authorship, they are known to preside. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ Conrad, bishop, we graciously assent to your just petitions. Following the example of Pope Eugenius, our predecessor of happy memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the church of Blessed Peter of Treviso, over which by God’s authorship you are known to preside; and we fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions or goods the same church now justly and canonically holds, or may hereafter [Col. 1284C] acquire, with the Lord’s aid, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names.

The church of Saint Mary of Asolo, with its castle, court, and all appurtenances; the monastery of Saint Mary of Muliano, etc. The remaining items are omitted, which are also read in the above-mentioned bull of Eugenius II.

> [Note: [Col. 1283D] See *Patrologia*, vol. CLXXX.]

The church of the Holy Forty [Martyrs], with its appurtenances; the hospital of Saint Julian of Fossapudia, with its appurtenances; the hospital of Aceto, with its appurtenances; the hospital of Mergara, with its appurtenances. We confirm by apostolic authority to you and your successors the appointment of monks and clerics belonging to the monastery of Narvisia, the monastery of Saint Fusca, [Col. 1284D] the monastery of Saint Martin, the monastery of Saint Fumia, the monastery of Cripignaga, the monastery of Saint Helena of Tessara—which is obliged to receive the bishop of Treviso on the feast-day of Saint Helena—and the monastery of Piro, as it is known to have been observed hitherto. The clerics of the aforesaid monasteries who minister to the people of the bishopric of Treviso must render obedience to the bishop of Treviso; and both abbots and their clerics must attend general chapters. The tithes of the mills of Plavi, from Negrisia as far as the sea; the church of Saint Stephen of Treviso; [Col. 1285A] the church of Saint Vitus; the church of Saint Augustine; the church of Saint Gregory; the hospital of Saint Leonard. We therefore decree, etc. If any person, etc.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Theodinus, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark, have subscribed. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Hubert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso, have subscribed. I, William, archbishop of Reims, cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina, [Col. 1285B] have subscribed. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore, have subscribed. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Soffredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Albinus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New, have subscribed.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Hugh, notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of October [1 October], in the third indiction, in the year 1184 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

## CLXIV. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the canons of Treviso.  
*(Verona, 1 October.)*

[Ibid., 533.]

[Col. 1285C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons OBERTO, dean of the church of Saint Peter of Treviso, and his brethren, present and future, canonically appointed: in perpetuity.

A petition of pious desire ought to be fulfilled by its resulting effect, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth worthily and the requested benefit may unquestionably receive its force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions. Following the example of our fathers and predecessors of sacred memory, Popes Eugenius and Alexander, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of Saint Peter, in which you are dedicated to divine service, [Col. 1285D] and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing.

We confirm by the authority of the Apostolic See the common life which you promised to observe in that church. We forbid any of you, after making that promise, to withdraw from it except on grounds of religion; and if anyone presumes to attempt this, he shall be deprived of the benefice of that church. Henceforth no one shall be instituted a canon in that church unless he has promised to observe this common life.

We decree that whatever possessions or goods that church now justly and canonically holds, or may hereafter acquire, with the Lord’s aid, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the tithes, offerings, first-fruits, burial dues, and the subjection of chaplains and clerics dwelling in the same city, as you have hitherto peacefully and canonically possessed them; the church of Saint Nicholas, situated within your cloister, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint John the Baptist; the church of Saint John of the Shore, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Bartholomew, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Sophia outside the walls of the city, with its appurtenances; lands within the city of Treviso, built upon and unbuilt; the enclosed ground which you possess beside the ditches of the same city; and the lands which you have in [lacuna] holdings [Col. 1286B] and the lands which you possess at Spauciano, Maltuco, Ursinico, and Bauliaco; the holdings which you possess at Castaniola; the holdings which you possess at Malsago, Postomia, and Musano; the church of Saint Bona, with its appurtenances and mills; the church of Saint Mary of Fontanis, with its appurtenances; and the land which you possess near the site of Pelagius of Spineta; the holdings which you possess at Lanzanigo, Braida, Maceraida, and Luvadina; the church of Saint Pelagius of Aurinis, with its appurtenances, the holdings which you possess in the same place, and the lands and tithes which you possess at Ponzano; the holdings which you possess at Paduano, Villa Orba, and at the foot of Montello; the holdings which you possess at Storga, Villa Pendula, and Salimbercu, and a place for constructing a mill; the holdings which you possess at Carbonara. [Col. 1286C]

The village of Melma, with the church of Saint Michael of that village and thirteen mill-wheels there, with their appurtenances; the holdings which you possess at Campo Storto, Lanzago, Cunfo, and Nerbono; the holdings which you possess at Luviniacum, Ripa Rupta, and Severa; and the lands which you possess at Fuligno; the holdings which you possess at Dulfon; the village and meadow of Gulzoli; the church of Saint Mary of that village, with its tithes and other appurtenances; one holding in Curte Natica; the lands which you possess at Mestre, built upon and unbuilt; the holdings which you possess at Zello, and the wood there; the land with vineyard which you possess at Cellarino; one holding at Brenulo and one holding at Canollata; the holdings which you possess at Burbiliaco; the lands which you possess at Podenzano, Scaltinico, and Carpino; the church of Saint Angel with its appurtenances; one holding at Mediolantiis; the church of Saint Gervasius with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Vitalis with its appurtenances, and the holdings which you possess there; the holdings which you possess at Zero; the holdings which you possess at Canizano and Reveno; the holdings which you possess at Quinto and Cervaria; the church of Saint Christina with its appurtenances, and the holdings which you possess there and at Tiverono; the church of Saint Andrew of Cavasagra, with its appurtenances; one holding at Puteo Bono; the holdings which you possess at Vedelago; the holdings which you possess in Silva Rotunda; the village of Silva Rosa, and the church of Saint Andrew situated in the same village, [Col. 1287A] with its appurtenances; the holdings which you possess at Sobiolla; the holdings which you possess at Bassano, Marmano, Romano, Burso, Canili, Saint Haria, Leudulis, Fonte, and Saint Zenone; the holdings which you possess at Asolo, Braida, Maliagello, and Nugaretto; the holdings which you possess at Montebelluna and its district; the lands which you possess at Triviniano, Casello, and Pusnovo; the holdings which you possess at Dupladino and Segusino, and one holding at Vipicano; the holdings which you possess at Petrarubea, Fenario, and Lano; the holdings which you possess at Auno and other places throughout the bishopric of Feltre; and the lands which you possess in the bishopric of Belluno, by the gift of Gregory, bishop of Treviso, of blessed memory; the entire tithe of all the land of Ciliano, whenever it is cultivated.

Moreover, all tithes in the territory of the city of Treviso known to have been assigned by right to the same church—as the aforementioned bishop granted to your said church and ratified by an authentic written instrument—we nonetheless confirm to you and, through you, to that church by apostolic authority. The parish church of Medulo, with the tithes you possess in that village; the church of Saint Margaret of Petrarubea, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Antolinus of Aspa; the holdings formerly belonging to Vidoro, canon; and the land of Grintina. [Col. 1287B]

Certainly, because the aforesaid goods were so alienated by certain provosts charged with the care of the goods of your canonry that you could scarcely be suitably maintained from them, in order to remove so great an inconvenience you, together with our venerable brother Conrad, your bishop, and certain of his predecessors, jointly decreed that one of your number should be chosen each year to administer the goods of that canonry for your benefit in the place of the provost. Assenting to your petitions, we confirm this constitution by apostolic authority, following the example of our predecessor Pope Alexander. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may, etc. But if anyone, etc.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theodinus, bishop of the see of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. [Col. 1287D] I, John, cardinal priest of Saint Mark. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus. I, William, archbishop of Reims, cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Hubert, cardinal priest of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. I, Gandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. [Col. 1288A] I, Soffredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Alberic, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Hugh, notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of October [1 October], in the third indiction, in the year 1184 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

## CLXV. He takes the monastery of Saint Peter of Vienne under protection.  
*(Fragment—Verona, 23 October.)*
