## CLXXXIV. He takes under protection the synagogue at Étampes, converted into the church of the Holy Cross after the Jews were expelled by Philip, king of the French. (Verona, 26 July.)

[FLEUREAU, *Les Antiquitez de la ville et du duchez d’Estampes*, quarto, p. 381.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the dean and canons of Holy Cross at Étampes: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Places devoted to divine worship, and which, after the blindness of Jewish unbelief, have received the light of grace under the title of the Christian faith, ought to be fortified by apostolic safeguards and endowed with the perpetual gift of freedom. For it is clear that those who have chosen there to serve the Lord in the freedom of the Spirit are now children not of the bondwoman but of the free woman. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of yours, which our dearest son in Christ Philip, illustrious king of the French, with the consent of our venerable brother G., archbishop of Sens, decreed should be built in honour of the most victorious Cross in the synagogue from which he had expelled the Jews. We fortify it by the protection of this present writing, together with all that it now justly and peacefully possesses or may hereafter reasonably acquire through the Lord’s favour [Col. 1316A].

We decree that clerics serving in the surrounding churches—just as, while Jews were possessors of that place, they received nothing from it—shall henceforth impose upon the church established there no condition or burden prejudicial to its freedom, lest the condition of the church become worse and that which had been free while Jews inhabited it become, under the observance of Christian liberty, a slave. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our protection or rashly act against it. If anyone presumes to attempt this, let that person know that he has incurred the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul [Col. 1316B].

Given at Verona, 26 July.

## CLXXXV. Privilege for the same church. (Verona, 8 August.)

[Ibid., p. 382.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the dean and canons of Holy Cross of Étampes: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since by the change wrought by the right hand of the Most High your church has been made from a Jewish synagogue, and a house of prayer has arisen where, a little before, the impious worship of the Jews was maintained, the duty of the administration entrusted to us induces us willingly to attend to your advancement and welfare and to grant your petitions an effect as ready as it is due [Col. 1316C]. Therefore, by apostolic authority we grant you leave to have, without any opposition, one master of the schools in music and another in the other disciplines. We decree that no one may presume to exact tithes from you of your newly cleared lands or of the fodder of your animals. We further forbid tithes to be demanded by laymen from your possessions.

Moreover, by the authority of these presents we decree that no one pronounce, without manifest and reasonable cause, a sentence of interdict against that church, or of excommunication or suspension against its canons. When a general interdict is imposed upon the land, you may, with doors closed, excommunicated and interdicted persons expelled [Col. 1316D], bells not rung, and voice subdued, celebrate the divine offices. We therefore decree, etc.

Given at Verona, 8 August.

## LXXXVI. Privilege for the brethren of St. Bertin of Saint-Omer. (Verona, 11 August.)

[Collection of Cartularies, III, 354.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbot and convent of St. Bertin: greeting and apostolic blessing.

When requests are made of the Apostolic See which do not depart from the path of reason, it is fitting for us readily to give consent and to fulfil the just wishes of petitioners by an effective result, so that sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the benefit sought may undoubtedly acquire force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, concurring favourably with your just requests, by these present letters we grant you, by apostolic authority, that in all your parishes you may appoint clerics who, with your assent and of your own will, shall hold the direction of the schools. We decree that this shall remain firm and inviolate for all time, and that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our concession or in any way act against it. If anyone presumes to attempt this, let that person know that he has incurred the indignation of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul [Col. 1317A].

Given at Verona, 11 August.

## CLXXXVII. Privilege for the monastery of Cour-Dieu. (Verona, 18 August.)

[*Gallia Christiana nova*, VIII, Documents, 522.]

[Col. 1317B]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, abbot, and the convent of Cour-Dieu: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although we ought in our justice to provide for all Christ’s faithful, we are more especially indebted to those who, having professed the religious life, have devoted themselves more strictly to divine service. Wishing, therefore, to provide for your freedom and rights, we confirm by apostolic authority the privileges granted to your monastery through the pious liberality and prudent concession of the kings of the French and bishops of Orléans, of illustrious memory [Col. 1317C]. But because the canons of Holy Cross challenge the bishops’ privileges, although those privileges contain the statement that the donations and liberties were granted to the abbey with the consent of the whole chapter, and although the privileges themselves are confirmed by the subscriptions of all persons, by apostolic authority we forbid them, on the ground that the seals of the chapter have not been attached to the privileges, to claim anything contrary to the tenor of those privileges to your prejudice.

Therefore no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our confirmation and prohibition or rashly act against it. If anyone presumes to attempt this, let that person know that he has incurred the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, 18 August.

## CLXXXVIII. He commands the dean of Le Mans, J. de Vieuxpont, archdeacon of Rouen, and Master Hugh of Janville to record the testimony of witnesses in the dispute between the churches of Dol and Tours. (Verona, 18 August.)

[MARTÈNE, *Thesaurus*, III, 910.]

[Col. 1317D]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the dean of Le Mans, J. de Vieuxpont, archdeacon of Rouen, and Master Hugh of Janville, provost of the church of St. Mary of the Castle: greeting and apostolic blessing.

When our beloved son, the bishop-elect of Dol, and the envoy of our venerable brother the archbishop of Tours, were present before us concerning the case which had long since arisen between them and their churches, had been litigated for a long time before Alexander, pope of happy memory, our predecessor, and in which he had committed the taking of witnesses of both parties under a specified form [Col. 1318A], after a long delay they jointly requested that we entrust to you three—the two chosen by the parties and the third appointed by us—the taking of witnesses according to the form prescribed by our said predecessor.

Considering that both churches had hitherto laboured fruitlessly at great expense and effort, we command your discretion by apostolic writings, and enjoin you by virtue of obedience, to proceed to a suitable place nearer to the church of Dol, secure for the archbishop or his procurator, to receive the witnesses of the church of Dol; and then to a safe place for the bishop-elect or his procurator, to receive the witnesses of the church of Tours. Setting aside all favour and fear, receive the witnesses of both parties according to the form prescribed by our predecessor within three months after receipt of these letters [Col. 1318B], notwithstanding any objection or appeal.

If either party is absent and does not send a procurator, unless it plainly proves a lawful impediment, we command that the witnesses of the party present be received under the sanctity of an oath, questioned with diligence, and that their statements be written down with every care and precaution. Then transmit the depositions, enclosed under your seals, to the Apostolic See [Col. 1318C], setting the parties a period of two months after the aforesaid three months during which the witnesses are to be received, within which they must appear before the apostolic presence with those depositions. Once the reasons of both parties, or of that party which has produced witnesses, have been seen and examined, the controversy shall receive its due conclusion, all evasion ceasing.

But if you cannot or will not attend to carrying this out, two of you shall execute the apostolic mandate, with all appeal and excuse set aside. Furthermore, if witnesses have not been received through the negligence of the judges or the delaying tactics of either party, nonetheless both parties, fully prepared, shall come to the Apostolic See at the appointed peremptory term which we assign to each party, either in person or through a sufficient advocate [Col. 1318D]. For if one comes and the other refuses to come, proceedings shall nevertheless go forward as reason dictates.

Given at Verona, 18 August.

## CLXXXIX. He commends the monastery of Follina to the bishops of the March of Treviso. (Verona, 23 August.)

[*Annales Camaldulenses*, IV, Appendix, p. 119.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brethren . . . bishop of Treviso [SIGIFRED], bishop of Ceneda [ARDONICUS], and the bishops of Feltre and Belluno [GERARD]: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more [lacuna] secular wickedness abounds and purity of religious life is rarer among them [Col. 1319A], the more attentively we must act and labour with utmost effort, so that, if any planting of pious life is raised there, it may be watered by you—who ought to be the waterers of such a planting—with the rains of timely consolation.

We have heard that the house of Follina, founded in those regions of yours under the profession of the Cistercian Order, though venerable for religion, nevertheless suffers from grievous poverty; and that certain magnates of your land harass it in many ways, extorting from it the few things which it possesses and imposing exactions upon it and its people under numerous compulsory services, from which even secular princes have customarily held sacred churches exempt. Therefore, by apostolic writings we command you [Col. 1319B] to rise manfully, as your office requires, against the perversity of this violence; to warn the magnates concerning whom such complaint comes to you to desist from this wrongdoing; and, if they do not obey the warning, to strike them with ecclesiastical censure—especially Jeremiah, who is said forcibly and unlawfully to hold two *mansi* belonging to that house, if the facts are so. Henceforth be so solicitous for the aforesaid monastery that the brethren who bear the service of divine warfare in it may be able fully to glory in you in the Lord.

Given at Verona, 23 August.

## CXC. He commands the archbishops and bishops established in the kingdom of the French to assist the monks of St. Denis in enforcing the monastery’s rights. (Verona, 25 August.)

[DOUBLET, *History of Saint-Denis*, vol. I, p. 518.]

[Col. 1319C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brethren, archbishops and bishops established in the kingdom of the French: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since the monastery of Blessed Denis has from times long past been held in great reverence, and since its care pertains especially to us, to whom it is subject without any intermediary, we are bound to defend it, through yourselves and the prelates of other churches, from the harassment of the wicked. This obligation is all the greater because, as the charity of many grows cold [Col. 1319D] and malice increases, there are many who continually trouble it with plunder and other molestations.

Therefore, wishing to oppose their wickedness and provide for its immunity from harm, we have delegated the affairs of that monastery to various judges for determination. We command your brotherhood, accordingly, that each of you in his own diocese, when requested, shall not delay in putting into execution—despite any appeal—the judgments which they deem necessary to pronounce in those affairs. Thus the monastery itself may more fully obtain its right through your office, and we, when we hear of your diligence, may deservedly commend it.

Given at Verona, 25 August.

## CXCI. He confirms to the Venetian convent of St. Zaccaria the property granted by Count Leonard. (Verona, 5 September.)

[CORNELII, *Ecclesiae Venetianae*, vol. XI, p. 381.]

[Col. 1320A]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, Caysota, abbess of St. Zaccaria of Venice, and the sisters of the same monastery: greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the tenor of a public instrument it has become known to us that, when Count Leonard of good memory made his testament, he appointed you, daughter abbess, as fiduciary trustee, trusting in your fidelity and religious character. To your monastery, for the remedy of his soul and those of his ancestors, he left in his last will all the vineyards, saltworks, lands [Col. 1320B], waters, cultivated and uncultivated lands, and the entire allod, however much he possessed in Clugia and its boundaries; and all things, movable and immovable, disposed of or undisposed of, together with all rights and actions which belonged or might belong to him against anyone, except those things which he had specifically bequeathed to named persons.

Since nothing is more owed to persons than that the expression of a final will, if it is reasonable, be free, we ratify the disposition of the aforesaid count and, by apostolic authority, confirm to you and to the same monastery all that he reasonably bestowed upon your monastery in his testament, fortifying it by the protection of this present writing [Col. 1320C]. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly act against it. If anyone presumes to attempt this, let that person know that he has incurred the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, 5 September.

## CXCII. He commands the bishop of Verona to order laymen to render tithes to the canons of Verona. (Verona, 11 September.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 800.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother, the bishop of Verona: greeting and apostolic blessing [Col. 1320D].

Since you ought especially to love our beloved sons the archpriest and canons of your church, and to uphold their rights with greater care, we direct these letters to you with the more confidence because we believe that you will more willingly obey apostolic commands. Therefore, by apostolic writings we command and enjoin your brotherhood to proceed by canonical censure, setting aside all favour and fear and notwithstanding any appeal, against all laymen who presume to take tithes from their revenues or summon them before a secular court concerning tithes. If, after warning, they do not desist, you shall not relax that censure without appropriate satisfaction.

Given at Verona, 11 September.

## CXCIII. He commands the bishops of Castello [Venice] and Torcello to compel certain parishioners of the church of St. Saviour to pay tithes. (Verona, 17 September.)

[CORNELII, *Ecclesiae Venetianae*, vol. XIV, p. 111.]

[Col. 1321A]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brethren, the bishops of Castello and Torcello: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved sons, the . . . prior and brethren of St. Saviour, have shown us by a communication that persons dwelling in houses adjudged to them by our venerable brother . . . patriarch of Grado and by Ildebrand of good memory, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and legate of the Apostolic See, refuse to acknowledge that they ought to be subject by parochial right [Col. 1321B] and to render them tithes. Wishing, therefore, to preserve unimpaired the rights of the same brethren, we command your brotherhood by apostolic writings to compel, through ecclesiastical censure and with the obstacle of appeal removed, the inhabitants of those houses to pay them tithes without difficulty according to the tenor of the apostolic privilege, and to make satisfaction for what has been withheld from the day on which the sentence was pronounced by our authority.

Given at Verona, 17 September.

## CXCIV. Privilege for the monastery of Reome. (Verona, 17 September.)

[D. PLANCHE, *History of Burgundy*, I, Proofs, p. 60.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbot and chapter of Reome: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily give consent to the just desires of petitioners and fulfil by effective result the wishes which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, concurring favourably with your just requests, we confirm by apostolic authority to your devotion, and fortify by the protection of this present writing, the church newly founded by our venerable brother, the bishop of Langres, beside the bridge of Montbard, in honour of Blessed Thomas the martyr. He granted it to you, with the consent of his chapter, in order that monks might be established there; and we confirm it as it was canonically bestowed upon you and as you canonically possess it with all its appurtenances [Col. 1321D]. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly act against it. If anyone presumes to attempt this, let that person know that he has incurred the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, 17 September.

## CXCV. Bull for the chapter of St. Martin of Tours. (Verona, 17 September.)

[Privileges of Saint-Martin of Tours, p. 25.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the dean, treasurer, and chapter of Blessed Martin of Tours: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1322A] Since the church of Blessed Martin of Tours is a special daughter of the Roman Church, we cannot fail to sympathize with all our affection in its burdens and to be moved with due severity against its wrongdoers. Having therefore heard that you pronounced an ecclesiastical sentence against your burgesses of Châteauneuf because of the commune, or common oath, which they had made to the detriment of that church and of yourselves, in accordance with the authority granted you by the Apostolic See, we decree that the same sentence is valid and confirm it by apostolic authority, willing that it be inviolably observed until full satisfaction is made to you and to the Church. Therefore no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly act against it. If anyone presumes to attempt this [Col. 1322B], let that person know that he has incurred the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, 17 September.

## CXCVI. Bull for the canons of St. Peter of Soissons. (Verona, 20 September.)

[D. GERMAIN, *History of Notre-Dame of Soissons*, 442.]

LUCIUS III, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, the abbess and convent of sisters of St. Mary of Soissons: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Those matters which pertain to the dignity of divine worship and are known to promote the welfare of churches ought to be granted by us with ready kindness and thereafter preserved in their stability [Col. 1322C]. Since, therefore, our beloved sons the canons of St. Peter of Soissons, according to the ancient observances of former times, are bound to serve in person at the altar of Blessed Mary, and since the granting of prebends belongs to you, daughter abbess, we decree and establish by the authority of these presents that, as this has been ordained and observed hitherto, none of those canons may transfer to parochial pastoral care without first relinquishing the prebend of your church, or undertake another title for which his service ought to be absent from the aforesaid altar.

Therefore no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our concession or rashly act against it. If anyone presumes to attempt this [Col. 1322D], let that person know that he has incurred the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, 20 September.

## CXCVII. He confirms to Arnald of Blois, canon of the church of Reims, the village of Fraillicourt. (Verona, 22 September.)

[VARIN, *Administrative Archives of Reims*, vol. I, part I, p. 397.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Master ARNALD of Blois, canon of the church of Reims: greeting and apostolic blessing . . .

Beloved son, concurring with your just petitions in gracious assent, we [Col. 1323A] confirm by apostolic authority to your devotion the estate of Fraillicurt, granted to you by our beloved sons R., provost, R., dean, Th., cantor, and the chapter of Reims, subject to the payment annually to the chapter of three pounds, taking account of your labour and of the profit arising from that labour, as you possess it peacefully and as is contained in the chapter’s authentic instrument. . . . The tenor of that instrument is as follows:

> “R., provost, R., dean, Th., cantor, and the other brethren of the Church of Reims, make known to all . . . that we have granted our estate of Fraillicurt, with all that may accrue there in our name, to be held for his lifetime by Master Arnald of Blois, our canon, subject to the payment annually to us of three pounds. Since he raised and improved that same estate, once poor [Col. 1323B] and humble, by a numerous population of inhabitants; since he also bought with his own money the fief which John of Ardennes held there—that is, two parts of the tithe of flax and land in the same village on which six or seven householders dwell; since he built anew a mill and ovens and made them manorial; and since he built there at his own expense and gave to us an excellent house and grange: we have granted him that his anniversary shall be solemnly observed.
>
> “Moreover, of all the goods of the aforesaid estate which, from our share, increase beyond the sum of eleven pounds, we have irrevocably ordained by the common assent of the chapter that one tenth part shall be distributed equally, on the day of his anniversary, for his soul and for the souls of all the faithful, among those present at the anniversary; that three poor persons shall especially be fed on the same day for that purpose; and that, further, on that day five solidi shall be expended from our purse at the guest-house, beyond the daily and customary fare, for a more generous visitation of the sick. [Col. 1323C] We have also ordained that the person who shall hold the aforesaid estate from us shall pay without delay, on the eve of the anniversary, the money raised from the aforesaid tenth on your behalf, and shall promise this without doubt, in the grant of the rent, upon the obligation of good faith.
>
> “And, that this may remain valid forever, we have strengthened it by the common assent of the chapter and by the protection of our seal.”

Therefore let no one, etc., etc.

[Col. 1323D] Given at Verona, 22 September.

## CXCVIII. Privilege for the monastery of Saint James at Liège.—He confirms to it the church of Saint Mary Magdalene. (Verona, 25 September.)

[MARTENE, *Amplissima Collectio*, I, 950.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and convent of Saint James of Liège, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has come to our knowledge by trustworthy report that the church of Blessed Mary Magdalene at Liège had once fallen, while under secular clerics, into such poverty that scarcely one among many could maintain an honourable livelihood there. Henry, of good memory, formerly bishop of Liège, [Col. 1324A] with the consent of the Church of Liège and of its founders, granted that church with its appurtenances to your monastery, established monks from that monastery in it for the perpetual celebration of divine service there, and confirmed his grant by his own written instrument.

Therefore, wishing to ratify what was reasonably done by him and has hitherto been observed, we confirm to you and to your monastery by apostolic authority that church with its appurtenances, as you possess it justly and peacefully by gift of the aforesaid bishop and as is contained in an authentic instrument; and we strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation [Col. 1324B] or in any way to oppose it. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, 25 September.

## CXCIX. He permits the monks of Saint Remigius, during general excommunications or interdicts, to celebrate offices behind closed doors. (Verona, 26 September.)

[VARIN, *Archives administratives de Reims*, vol. I, pt. I, p. 398.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and monks of Blessed Remigius of Reims, etc.

By this present document we have thought fit to decree that, [Col. 1324C] when a general interdict of the land is in force, you may celebrate the divine offices with the doors closed, excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded, bells not rung, and in a low voice.

Given at Verona, 26 September.

## CC. He confirms the customs and liberties of the citizens of Reims, established by Archbishop William. (Verona, 1 October.)

[VARIN, ibid., p. 405.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons and the citizens of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Those measures which are established, through the zealous effort of pious intention, by persons set in high office for strengthening the bond of peace ought to remain firm, and to receive enduring force through the favour of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, concurring with your just petitions in gracious assent, we decree to be valid the honourable customs and reasonable liberties which our venerable brother William, archbishop of Reims, cardinal of Saint Sabina and legate of the Apostolic See, granted you for the preservation of peace and for the maintenance of justice and equity, and which both he and our beloved son in Christ Philip, illustrious king of the Franks, confirmed by authentic instrument. At the intervention especially of the aforesaid archbishop, we also confirm them to you by apostolic authority [Col. 1325A] as they are contained in the authentic documents, and strengthen them by the protection of this present writing. Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly oppose it. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, 1 October.

## CCI. Privilege for the abbot and monks of Laach. (Verona, 16 October.)

[GUNTHER, *Codex diplomaticus Rheno-Mosellanus*, I, 446.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and brethren of Laach, greeting and apostolic [Col. 1325B] blessing.

Since the life of subjects is instructed by the conduct of their prelates, it is fitting and consonant with reason that, when the devotion of a people asks that religious men be placed over them as pastors, ready consent should be granted to its pious desires. Since it has thus come to the hearing of our apostolic office that a certain parish church of Crufthe, belonging to your monastery, requests to be governed by you or by other religious men, we grant you by the authority of this present document that, whenever that church is vacant, you may appoint in it three or four of your brethren, one of whom shall be presented to the bishop and, receiving the cure of souls from the bishop, shall be accountable to him in spiritual matters and to you in temporal matters. Therefore let no person whatsoever [Col. 1325C] be permitted to infringe this page of our grant or rashly oppose it. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, 16 October.

## CCII. To Walter, archbishop of Rouen.—No one is to be instituted in churches unless he is a priest, or will shortly become one, and is prepared to reside there; nor are less suitable persons to be accepted, even if presented by patrons. (Verona, 16 October.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXII, 479.]

LUCIUS, bishop . . . to WALTER, [Col. 1325D] archbishop of Rouen . . . .

Since it is often said to occur in your archbishopric that the institution in churches there of unsuitable persons causes scandal and hardship, we wish you to be diligent and attentive, so that, God willing, those churches may in your time be so ordered that clerical honour remains unimpaired and the condition of the churches is continuously preserved intact.

Therefore, by these present letters we forbid your brotherhood to admit as vicars of parish churches anyone except persons who either are priests or ought shortly to become priests, and who are willing and able to serve those churches in person.

Furthermore, you shall consent that the cure of souls be entrusted to no one unless he can and ought to be advanced to priestly orders within the period fixed by the sacred canons. But if the patrons of churches do not present suitable persons to you, you may, by our authority and without impediment of appeal, appoint suitable ministers in those churches, to whom the welfare of the churches may beneficially be entrusted in both spiritual and temporal matters. [Col. 1326A]

Therefore let no one, etc.

Given at Verona, 16 October.

## CCIII. He grants the clerics of Osnabrück the power to make a testament. (Verona, 22 October.)

[MOSER, *Osnabrückische Geschichte*, IV, 109.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1326B] sons, the clerics of the Church of Osnabrück, greeting and apostolic blessing.

By the apostolic office entrusted to us by God, we are bound to provide for the right and welfare of clerics and to grant them our stronger protection against assaults of wrongdoing. On your behalf, indeed, it has been reported to us that laymen, on the ground of kinship, rashly infringe testaments made concerning your own property, not allowing them to be carried out in accordance with the will of those making the dispositions. Wishing therefore to provide for you in this matter with paternal concern, we grant to your discretion by the authority of this present document that henceforth you shall have free power to make testaments concerning any of your own property, according to the enactments of laws and canons. [Col. 1326C] By our apostolic authority we strictly forbid anyone to presume in any way, on the ground of kinship, to violate your canonically made testaments. Let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our command and prohibition or rashly oppose it. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the excommunication of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, 22 October.

## CCIV. He confirms to the monastery of Cluny an estate granted by Jocerannus Grossus. (Verona, 23 October.)

[*Bullarium Cluniacense*, 77.]

[Col. 1326D]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and convent of Cluny, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners, and bring to effective completion the requests which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, concurring with your just petitions in gracious assent, we confirm to you and to your monastery by apostolic authority, and strengthen by the protection of this present writing, the place which the nobleman Jocerannus Grossus, with his wife’s consent, granted to you by pious gift from his own allodial estate and woodland of Gron, where a church built in honour of Saint John the Evangelist is known to stand, according to the boundary limits contained in his authentic instrument, and as you justly and peacefully possess that place with its appurtenances. [Col. 1327A] Therefore let no one, etc.

Given at Verona, 23 October.

## CCV. To Ralph, bishop of Angers. (Verona, 27 October.)

[MORICE, *Mémoires pour servir à l’histoire de Bretagne*, I, 699.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother, the bishop of Angers, and to his beloved sons G., archdeacon, and J., archpriest of Tours, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more especially the monastery of Saint Florentius of Saumur [Col. 1327B] is held to belong to us and to blessed Peter, the more grievous it ought to be to us when we hear that its rights are diminished through anyone’s rashness. You should know that it has been laid before us that the abbey of Saint Melanius of Redon is so dependent upon the monastery of Saumur that the monks of the one are brethren of the other, and that no abbot ought to be appointed there except with the agreement of the abbot of Saumur and chosen from among the monks of that other monastery. Yet a certain man, brought in from elsewhere through the power of the nobleman G., count of Brittany, has been intruded into the aforesaid monastery of Saint Melanius, despite the objections of the aforesaid abbot of Saumur and the brethren, and seeks to hold that monastery to their detriment. Since, therefore, what was wickedly done in that abbey should be restored to the path of rectitude, we have enjoined and commanded your discretion by apostolic letters that, summoning both parties before you, you hear the arguments and allegations advanced on either side and settle the case through justice. [Col. 1327C]

Given at Verona, 27 October.

## CCVI. He confirms to the monastery of Altenberg the estate of Isacherode. (Verona, 29 October.)

[LACOMBLET, *Urkundenbuch*, I, 347.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and brethren of Altenberg, greeting and [Col. 1327D] apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners and bring to effective completion requests which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, concurring with your just petitions in gracious assent, we confirm to you and to your monastery by apostolic authority, and strengthen by the protection of this present writing, the allodial estate of the village of Isacherode with all its appurtenances, in the immunity and integrity in which William of Solebendorp and his wife, with the consent and will of their sons, gave it to you out of devotion for the salvation of their souls, and as you justly and peacefully possess it. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our [Col. 1328A] confirmation or rashly oppose it. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, 29 October.

## CCVII. He grants Maurice, bishop of Paris, that fiefs of the bishopric of Paris may not be pledged or sold without his consent. (Verona, 30 October.)

[*Poenitentiale of Theodore*, II, 638.]

LUCIUS, to MAURICE, bishop of Paris.

The merit of your devotion and integrity is shown to require that what is owed to others by common right should be granted, through the office which we exercise, to your brotherhood—which humbly and devoutly requests it—by the special generosity of an indulgence. Therefore, venerable brother in the Lord, by these present letters we grant you that no ecclesiastical or secular person may presume, under any authority, to take in pledge or purchase your fiefs without your consent. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur both the loss arising from his contract and our indignation. [Col. 1328B]

Given at Verona, 30 October.

## CCVIII. He grants to the abbots of the monastery of Saint George in the Black Forest the use of the mitre, gloves, and sandals. (Verona, 31 October.)

[GERBERT, *Codex diplomaticus Historiae Silvae Nigrae*, p. 109.]

[Col. 1328C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son MANEGALD, abbot of Saint George in the Black Forest, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since your monastery, over which by God’s appointment you are known to preside, belongs especially to blessed Peter and flourishes in the discipline of regular observance, it is fitting that we should give special attention to your honour, upon whom rests the burden of administering that monastery, and to that of those who, by the Lord’s generosity, shall succeed you in the same charge; and that, so far as we can in the Lord, we should grant your pious desires the wished-for favour in the Lord of an indulgence from the Apostolic See. Moved by this consideration, and likewise persuaded by the affectionate prayers of our venerable brother Gotefrid, patriarch of Aquileia, who petitioned us on your and your church’s behalf, we grant and confirm by the protection of this present writing to you and to your canonical successors the use of the mitre, gloves, and sandals on the principal solemnities, both in the solemn celebration of Mass and in the possessions of your church, through the clemency of the Apostolic See. [Col. 1328D] Let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe the page of our confirmation or rashly oppose it. If anyone should presume to attempt anything contrary to this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, 31 October.

## CCIX. To Philip, archbishop, and B., provost, of Cologne. (Verona, 31 October.)

[GUNTHER, *Codex diplomaticus Rheno-Mosellanus*, I, 447.]

[Col. 1329A]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother PH., archbishop, and to his beloved son B., provost of Cologne, greeting and apostolic blessing.

A complaint sent to us by our beloved daughters in Christ, the mistress and nuns of Dünwald, has revealed that the abbot and brethren of the church of Laach presume unreasonably to harass them concerning the payment of tithes from nine holdings, from which they are exempt according to the privileges of the Roman pontiffs [Col. 1329B] and for which they pay the diocesan bishop the due right. Therefore we command your discretion by apostolic letters to compel the aforesaid brethren of the church of Laach, by ecclesiastical censure and without obstacle of appeal, to render full justice to the said nuns.

Given at Verona, 31 October.

## CCX. He commands the bishop of Senigallia not to allow the privileges of the Church of Ravenna to be infringed. (Verona, 4 November.)

[RUBEI, *Historia Ravennatis*, p. 356.]

[Col. 1329C] LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother . . . bishop of Senigallia, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since by the office entrusted to us we are debtors to all churches, we are bound to assist Ravenna the more particularly because it was founded earlier in the confession of the Christian name, presides over many, and advances salvation. Since, therefore, in your bishopric and elsewhere its rights are disturbed by many persons, as a result of which it is known to have been considerably diminished in its possessions through the malice of the wicked, we exhort your brotherhood in the Lord and command you that you give it prompt and diligent assistance in its just claims, and that you compel your parishioners, concerning whom complaint has been brought to you, by sentence of excommunication and without appeal, not to delay in rendering to the archdeacon and brethren of that church the full measure of justice in all matters which they demand. [Col. 1329D]

Given at Verona, 4 November.

## CCXI. He confirms to the convent of Saint Remigius of Reims the tithe of Besenes and certain privileges. (Verona, 8 November.)

[VARIN, *Archives administratives de Reims*, vol. I, pt. I, p. 406.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and convent of Saint Remigius . . . . .

Concurring with your petitions in gracious assent, we confirm to you by apostolic authority what you justly and peacefully [Col. 1330A] hold or possess in the tithe of Besenes. Moreover, by these present letters we grant you that, as is reasonably contained in the authentic instrument of our venerable brother, the archbishop of Reims [W.], cardinal of Saint Sabina and legate of the Apostolic See, no one may release a sentence canonically pronounced against your wrongdoers without promised fitting satisfaction or sufficient security for obedience to the Church’s command. We further decree that householders of the villages of Saint Remigius, should they choose to depart elsewhere, remain liable for payment of the proceeds and rents and for the burdens of the lands, unless they freely choose to leave the lands behind, as is canonically expressed in the same privilege of the aforesaid archbishop of Reims. [Col. 1330B]

Moreover, since twelve canons are appointed in the church of Saint Timothy, we decree by this present document that henceforth they shall either serve in person the benefices granted to them or, if they determine to be absent, appoint suitable vicars to serve in their stead; otherwise, by this present indulgence, we grant you free power to confer their benefices upon others who will serve. Decreeing that no one whatsoever, etc. . . .

Given at Verona, 8 November.

## CCXII. He confirms, between the same church and the monastery of Saint Denis, a judgment concerning a prebend of the church of Saint Exuperius of Corbeil, delivered by J., formerly bishop of Chartres. (Verona, 13 November.)

[DOUBLET, *History of Saint-Denis*, vol. I, p. 515.]

[Col. 1330C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and monks of blessed Denis, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Matters settled by judgment or reasonable agreement ought fittingly to remain firm and unimpaired; and, lest they be disturbed by anyone’s malice, they ought to be committed to written record and secured by apostolic protection. Since a controversy had arisen between your monastery and the church of Saint Exuperius of Corbeil concerning the entirety of a prebend in that church, which you asserted belonged by right to the priory of Blessed Mary of the Fields, J., formerly bishop of Chartres, of good memory, to whom the case had been committed by apostolic mandate, made this settlement between you: that whoever at any time should be prior in the aforesaid church of Saint Mary of the Fields should receive the whole prebend and serve it through a vicar. In that same church he shall celebrate the principal Mass there on the feast of Saint Exuperius, or, if he prefers, shall cause it to be celebrated by another. [Col. 1330D]

Therefore we confirm by apostolic authority what the bishop decreed concerning that prebend, as it was reasonably done and as is more fully contained in the said bishop’s written instrument, and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our [Col. 1331A] confirmation or rashly oppose it. If anyone should, etc.

Given at Verona, 13 November.

## YEAR 1185.

## CCXIII. He congratulates Baldwin, archbishop of Canterbury, on the office he has assumed, and sends him the pallium through his notary Transmundus.

[TWYSDEN, *Historiae Anglicanae Scriptores*, vol. I, p. 627.]

The more fully the fragrance of your praiseworthy manner of life and the reputation of your proven uprightness have long since reached our knowledge, the more greatly do we and our brethren rejoice in the Lord [Col. 1331B] and render thanks to almighty God, because, looking upon the church of Canterbury with His customary mercy, He has called you to govern it. You, who had been proved in many things and found faithful, ascend to higher things at the Lord’s invitation, refreshing many unto salvation by the fragrance of your virtues; and your commendable deeds will shine more precious because you have attained a more eminent rank of dignity.

For we believe that this has been done by the Lord and is acceptable in our eyes: the divinely inspired desires of all agreed in your election, and with one mouth and harmonious voices declare you most worthy of the summit of dignity to which, like Aaron, you have been called by God. Accordingly, we received with cheerful mind and due kindness the envoys of royal excellency and the prudent and discerning men both of the suffragans and of the chapter of the church of Canterbury. Having learned from the letters which they bore and from their own report that your election was canonical and approved by God and men, after deliberation with our brethren we took care to confirm it with fitting promptness and favour. Moreover, we granted your brotherhood the pallium, the fullness of the pontifical office, and have caused it to be sent through our beloved son Transmundus, our notary and household officer, nurtured beneath our wings from ancient times. [Col. 1331C]

## CCXIV. Privilege granted to the Carthusian prior and all brethren of the order. (Verona, 8 January.)

[*Privileges of the Carthusian Order*, fol. 2b.]

[Col. 1331D]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the Carthusian prior and all brethren of the same order, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more fervently you labour, by God’s enabling, in regular observance, the more sincerely we love your whole community and ought, and wish, to provide more attentively for your peace. Therefore, granting your petitions, we allow you by apostolic authority that, if at times of ordination you have sought your diocesan bishop but are unable to have access to him, you may invite another Catholic bishop, concerning whose ordination no harm need be feared by your own prelate; he may, by our authority, grant what you request. Let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our grant or rashly oppose it. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul. [Col. 1332A]

Given at Verona, 8 January.

## CCXV. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Ghislain. (Verona, 12 January.)

[REIFFENBERG, *Monuments*, VIII, 396.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons LAMBERT, abbot of the monastery of Saint Ghislain, [Col. 1332B] and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

Both the force of equity and the order of reason require that just petitioners be granted effective relief, especially where piety assists the petitioners’ wishes and truth is not forsaken. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just petitions; we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and secure it by the privilege of this present writing.

First, we decree that the monastic order known to have been established in that monastery according to God and the Rule of Saint Benedict shall be observed there inviolably in perpetuity. Further, whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God willing, through the grants of pontiffs, the gifts of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with all its appurtenances; the village of Hornut with its appurtenances; in the village of Slogia, the demesne manor and one ploughland of arable land with enclosed holdings, and the entire tithe both of that land itself and of all the fiefs of the same village, and of cultivated as well as uncultivated lands; from the manor of Saint Peter, [Col. 1332D] the tithes as you have held them hitherto; the tithe from Hugh’s vineyard; the hamlet called Ultra Montes, with its appurtenances, and the church of that place with its dependencies at Arminiac and Bewermies; the tithe of the manor and lands of Saint Landelinus; at Novella, one ploughland of arable land; one fourth of the village of Blelgiis with its appurtenances and jurisdiction; in the village called Wamia, the allod of Gonther and of his son Aegidius of Cing, and the land of Hugh of Aengien, with other lands, enclosed holdings, rents, meadows, and woods; a part of the village of Durni with the village and jurisdiction; the village of Waherias and the demesne manor, free from every advocacy and tithe; the church which you possess from the church of Saint Gaugericus under an annual rent of one hundred solidi in Cambrai currency; [Col. 1333A] in the village of Chavren, the demesne manor with lands, meadows, waters, woods, and enclosed holdings, and a portion of the tithe, free from every lordship and separated from the other shares; in the village called Harcheiis, three fertons by the weight of Flanders, owed by the church of Alnes for the land of Heluidis; at Resbaco, the demesne manor and three parts of the entire allod, in lands, woods, waters, meadows, rents, and jurisdiction.

At Runcherias, six marks of silver by the weight of Cologne, owed under an annual rent by the church of Cambron for the lands of that place, and the altar with the chapel of Herieriponte; the altar of Cella with its appurtenances Blelgiis, Hercana, Astices, and Slogio; the church of Willari with its appurtenances Harminiac and Beweniis; the church of Wamiis with its appurtenances Wamiolo and Resiniis; Bassecles with its appurtenances; Altregium with the village chapel, with all its appurtenances, free from every exaction except the bishop’s entertainment allowance. At Imbrechiis, the manor and demesne lands with meadows and waters, and two parts of the common allod free from every exaction; the altar of Bossut, free from the *personatus* and every exaction, except an annual payment of six denarii for the bishop’s entertainment allowance; the altar of Baldurno with its dependency Villerot, free from every exaction except an annual payment of three solidi for the bishop’s entertainment allowance; the altars of Eligniis and Tumaides; the chapel of Ramegniis, free from the *personatus* and every exaction except the bishop’s entertainment allowances; Abeceias with its appurtenances Belchi, Molembais, Popiola, Petrewez, [Col. 1333C] and its other appurtenances; also the altars granted to you by Nicholas, of good memory, formerly bishop of Cambrai, and confirmed by his privileges; Harceiis with its appurtenances Grandi Ecclesia and Stambrusia, and the chapel of Equi-campus; the altar of Blato, free and without a *personatus*; the chapel of Weltes, free except for the *sonegium* of twelve denarii; the altar of Thulin with its dependency Hainin; the altar of Hunceniis; the altar of Herseela; the altar of Rascengen; the altar of Humberges; the altar of Goi with its land and other appurtenances; the altar of Lovegniis with its appurtenances Dolziis and the chapel of Squeri; the chapel of Fait and the chapel of Herieriponte, free from every exaction and *personatus*.

In the village of Alemannis, the demesne manor and the tithe of that manor and of the land belonging to that village, in lands, vineyards, meadows, woods, and whatever you justly and peacefully possess in the district of Soissons; the manor and demesne lands at Altregium, and shares of the common allod in lands, waters, meadows, woods, and rents, free from every exaction and advocacy; the village of Bassecles with all its appurtenances, and the administration of that village granted to your monastery in alms, with the liberties and appurtenances which the aforesaid benefices are known to have. [Col. 1333D]

Certainly, no one shall presume to demand or exact tithes from you on your newly cleared lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or upon the sustenance of your animals. You may also receive into conversion clerics or laymen fleeing from the world, if free and absolved, and retain them without any opposition. Whenever a general interdict of the land is in force, you may celebrate divine offices, with doors closed, excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded, bells not rung, and voices subdued. We also decree that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while preserving nevertheless the right of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken.

When you, the present abbot of that place, or any of your successors dies, no one shall be set over it by any craft of intrigue or violence, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the wiser part of the brethren, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict. We also confirm by apostolic authority the ancient and reasonable customs, liberties, and immunities reasonably granted to that monastery and hitherto observed. Further, we forbid anyone to dare to pronounce against you or your churches a sentence of excommunication or interdict without manifest and reasonable cause. [Col. 1334B]

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of diocesan bishops.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowingly acting against this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt anything contrary to it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject at the final judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus. I, Hubert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Theodinus, bishop of the see of Porto and Saint Rufina. [Col. 1335A] I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Joffred, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Albinus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary Nova.

Given at Verona through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the second Ides of January, in the third indiction, in the year 1184 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

CCXVI. He permits John, prior, and the brothers of the Valley of Saint John of Seitz to invite any bishop to confer orders, should the diocesan bishop be unavailable at the time of ordination. (Verona, January 23.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXII, 479.]

[Col. 1335B]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons JOHN, prior, and the brothers of the Valley of Saint John: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more zealously, by God’s working, you labour in regular observance, the more sincerely we love your whole community, and the more attentively we ought and desire to provide for your peace. Therefore, assenting to your requests, by apostolic authority we [Col. 1335C] grant you that, if at the times of ordinations you are unable to obtain the services of the diocesan bishops, you may invite another Catholic bishop, whom the diocesan prelate need not fear will, on the occasion of such an ordination, wish to extend the boundaries of his bishopric into another’s jurisdiction and diminish those of the diocesan bishop. When invited, he shall, by our authority, grant what you request; nor may he thereafter demand this from you as though it were a right due to him.

Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our concession or, by rash daring, to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

[Col. 1335D] Given at Verona, on the tenth day before the Kalends of February.

CCXVII. He commends the monastery of Rott to Archbishop Adalbert of Salzburg and his suffragans. (Verona, February 20.)

[*Monumenta Boica*, vol. I, p. 368.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable N., bishop of Salzburg, and to his suffragans: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although, by reason of the office of administration imposed upon us, we are bound to extend apostolic protection against the attacks of the wicked to all the Churches of God, yet we ought to give more diligent assistance to religious foundations subject to rule and belonging immediately to us and to the Roman Church, and to call upon our brother bishops for the preservation of their [Col. 1336A] rights. Therefore, since the monastery of Rott, which belongs in a special manner to blessed Peter and to our jurisdiction, is often harassed by many troubles, we have thought it right to commend it earnestly to your brotherhood. By these apostolic letters we command and enjoin that, whenever a complaint is brought before you, or any one of you, concerning investitures of churches, loss of its possessions, or other oppressions inflicted by others, you shall hear them mercifully and, by ecclesiastical censure and without impediment of appeal, compel the wrongdoers to cease harassing them and to restore the things taken away, as justice requires. Thus the brothers dwelling there may, through your solicitude, serve the Lord in peace; and when we hear of it, we [Col. 1336B] shall take it gratefully.

Given at Verona, on the tenth day before the Kalends of March.

CCXVIII. He receives the Church of Saint Mary at Regensburg under protection and confirms its rights. (Verona, February 27.)

[RIED., *Codex diplomaticus Ratisbonensis*, I, 263.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ERBORD, dean, and the canons of Saint Mary at Regensburg, called the Old Chapel, both present and future, canonically appointed in perpetuity.

A devout petition ought to be fulfilled by a corresponding effect, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth worthily and the requested benefit may assuredly [Col. 1336C] acquire force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and, following the example of Pope Alexander of happy memory, our predecessor, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid Church of Saint Mary at Regensburg, called the Old Chapel, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, God granting, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper [Col. 1336D] names: the churches situated upon your estate, namely Rotigen with its appurtenances; the church of Nitenowe with its appurtenances; the church of Cydelarn with its appurtenances; the church of Phaphenchoven with its appurtenances; the church of Mosheym with its appurtenances; the church of Aeuningen with its appurtenances; the estate of Wolfhartstorf with its appurtenances; the court situated in the suburb of the city with its appurtenances; the court of Helkeringen with four vineyards; five vineyards on the hill belonging to the prebend, and six belonging to the offering, with their appurtenances; and also the tithes of all vineyards situated within your territory.

We further decree that, upon the death of your provost, whoever he may be at the time, no one shall be placed over you by the craft of secret intrusion or by violence, except one whom [Col. 1337A] the brethren, by common consent, or the sounder judgment of the brethren’s party, shall provide to be elected according to God. We also prohibit the provost from personally giving or leasing to anyone any courts, tithes, holdings, or other benefice belonging to your church, or alienating them in any other way, without the common consent of the chapter or of its greater and sounder part. Nor shall he convert any of the church’s goods to his own use before the brothers’ prebend has been fully distributed, as was established of old, and entrusted for distribution to a cellarer whom the brothers have chosen as useful and faithful to themselves.

Moreover, he shall presume to claim nothing for himself from offerings that are not his by right; rather, the chamberlain of offerings, who is specially charged by ancient and reasonable institution with preserving and distributing them, shall dispense them with due provision. From the brothers’ wine or beer he shall take nothing except what he knows belongs to his portion according to the custom of your church. Furthermore, we prohibit the provost from granting your churches contrary to justice to any priest by his authority alone; rather, sitting in chapter with the dean and the other brethren, he shall choose a priest of honourable conduct and present the chosen man, together with the other elders, to the bishop. Having received the care of souls from him, that priest shall be answerable to him in spiritual matters and to you in temporal matters.

By apostolic authority we likewise judge it necessary to prohibit your advocate from presuming to burden the place itself, or its dependencies, or to harass them with any unlawful exactions; rather, he shall be content with those things granted to him in ancient times [Col. 1337C] and belonging to his lawful right. We further decree that the burial-place of that establishment shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have determined to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken remaining unimpaired. All these things, therefore, as they were established and observed of old, we confirm to you and, through you, to that Church by apostolic authority.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; [Col. 1337D] but that all things shall be preserved whole for the use and benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop being preserved. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by due satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject to divine vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place may there be the peace of the Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit [Col. 1338A] of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theodinus, bishop of Porto and the see of Saint Rufina. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Arditio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Goffred, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Albinus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary Nova. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus.

Given at Verona through the hand of Albert, [Col. 1338B] cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Kalends of March, in the year 1184 of the Lord’s Incarnation and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

Lead seal. LUCIUS POPE III.

CCXIX. Privilege for the monastery of Raitenhaslach and the other monasteries of the Cistercian order. (Verona, March 4.)

[*Monumenta Boica*, III, 116.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable archbishops and bishops, and to his beloved sons the abbots, priors, and other prelates of churches to whom these letters shall come: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1338C] We have heard, and in hearing have been deeply moved with astonishment, that although it has been granted to the brothers of Raitenhaslach, as to all others of the Cistercian order, by our brethren and predecessors, and afterwards confirmed by ourselves, that they are not obliged to pay tithes to anyone from the produce which they cultivate by their own hands or at their own expense, certain persons presume to extort such tithes from them and, by a perverse interpretation of the chapter in apostolic privileges, assert that where “produce” (*labores*) is written, “newly cultivated lands” (*novalia*) ought to be understood. Since it is manifest to all who think rightly that this interpretation is perverse and contrary to sound understanding, and since under that chapter they are altogether exempt from paying tithes both from lands which they have brought or bring [Col. 1338D] under cultivation and from cultivated lands which they till by their own hands or at their own expense, we command and enjoin you by apostolic letters, lest anyone have material for maligning them or harassing them in any way contrary to justice, diligently to prohibit all persons subject to your authority from presuming in any manner to extort tithes from the said brothers of Raitenhaslach, or from brothers of other monasteries of the Cistercian order situated in your bishoprics, whether from newly cultivated lands, other lands cultivated by their own hands or at their own expense, or the produce of their animals. For if we had intended “newly cultivated lands” alone where we write “produce,” we would have written “newly cultivated lands,” as [Col. 1339A] we do in the privileges of certain others.

But because it is unfitting that the enactments of the Apostolic See, which ought to retain inviolable force, should be rashly violated, we command and enjoin everywhere by apostolic letters that, if any canons, clerics, monks, or laymen burden the aforesaid brothers by demanding tithes contrary to the privileges of the Apostolic See, you shall, appeal being set aside, strike the laymen with a sentence of excommunication and suspend the others from their office; and you shall cause both the excommunication and suspension to be observed inviolably until due satisfaction has been made. Moreover, by the authority of these presents we command and enjoin you that, if any persons lay violent hands upon brothers of the aforesaid monasteries, you shall publicly announce them as excommunicated with lighted candles [Col. 1339B] and cause all persons to avoid them strictly as excommunicates, until they have made suitable satisfaction to the aforesaid brothers and presented themselves before the apostolic presence with letters of the diocesan bishop setting forth the truth of the matter.

Given at Verona, on the fourth Nones of March, in the third [fourth] year of our pontificate.

CCXX. He receives the monastery of Paris in the district of Alsace under protection and confirms its goods. (Verona, March 12.)

[HUGO, *Sacred Monuments of Antiquity*, vol. II, p. 282.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1339C] sons Wezilo, abbot of the monastery of Paris in the district of Alsace, and his brothers, both present and future, professing the regular life in perpetuity.

It is fitting that apostolic protection should be present for those who choose the religious life, lest the assault of any rash person either draw them away from their purpose or, which God forbid, weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery of Paris, situated in the district of Alsace, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document.

[Col. 1339D] First, indeed, we decree that the monastic order recognized as established in that monastery according to God, the Rule of blessed Benedict, and the institution of the Cistercian brothers, shall there be observed inviolate for all time.

Furthermore, whatever possessions or goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, God granting, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, together with all [Col. 1340A] its appurtenances: Kinuelden, Lehem, Scheferwald, Arcenhem, Mochenhem, Egensheim, Forst, Mitelwilre, Kolmere, Als Paris, Rumimunt, Chazinthale, Tambach, Scrotegin, Pfaffenhem, Ruvache, and Herlishem, with all their appurtenances.

Moreover, let no one presume to demand or extort from you tithes from the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the increase of your animals.

You are also permitted to receive into conversion clerics or laymen fleeing the world, who are free and unencumbered, and to retain them without any opposition. We further prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, [Col. 1340B] from leaving it without his abbot’s permission; and no one shall dare retain a departing brother without letters of the community certifying the matter.

Furthermore, by apostolic authority we decree that, as was established by our predecessors of happy memory, the Roman pontiffs Innocent, Eugenius, and Alexander, no bishop or any other person shall compel you against your will to attend synods or secular assemblies.

We also decree that if the bishop in whose parish your house is founded, when humbly and devoutly requested three times at intervals, should perhaps refuse to bless an abbot who has been appointed, that abbot may lawfully bless his own novices and exercise the other functions belonging to his office [Col. 1340C] until that bishop reconsiders his hardness and no longer refuses to bless the abbot presented for blessing.

Wishing also to provide with paternal solicitude for your peace and tranquillity, we prohibit by apostolic authority anyone, within the enclosures of your sites or granges, from daring to commit violence, robbery, or theft, set fire, seize a person, or kill one.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, let all things be preserved whole for the use and benefit of those for whose [Col. 1340D] governance and support they were granted, the authority of the Apostolic See being preserved.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by due satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject to divine vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good [Col. 1341A] action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Nine cardinals have subscribed: namely, three bishops, three priests, and three deacons.

Given at Verona through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fourth Ides of March, in the third indiction, in the year 1184 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

CCXXI. To William, bishop of Poitiers—Concerning the correction of certain abuses in the diocese of Poitiers, etc. (Verona, March 13.)

[MARTÈNE, *Treasury*, 620.]

[Col. 1341B]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother WILLIAM, bishop of Poitiers: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since it was established at the Lateran council, in order to restrain the excessive avarice of certain persons and remove grounds for disputes, that ecclesiastical benefices should not be promised before they become vacant, it is grievous and troublesome to us that abbots and priors in your diocese are reported to pass by wholesome enactments with deaf ears and there make unlawful promises of this kind. Therefore, lest this enormity, which had been cut off by a salutary constitution, should regain strength through dissimulation and once more grow into a pernicious licence, [Col. 1341C] we grant you by these letters that, such promises being annulled, if, owing to disputes which frequently arise from this source through the fault of those known to have the right of presentation, churches should happen to remain vacant for more than six months, you may, by authority of the Apostolic See and without prejudice to their rights in the future, provide them with suitable persons, all contradiction or appeal being set aside. We do not, however, wish the greater churches or the reverence due to them to be diminished by this.

Also, in order that you may carry out the office entrusted to you more freely, seeing that apostolic protection is at hand, we grant by this authority to your solicitude that you may correct, with the counsel of our beloved sons the abbots of Saint Cyprian and of Pinu, abbesses and other women known to preside over religious houses in your bishopric, through whose inadequacy [Col. 1341D] and negligence women devoted to God depart from religious observance. If they are found contumacious, you may restrain them by ecclesiastical discipline without recourse to appeal, so that, where the fomentations of remedies are not felt, festering wounds may be cut away by the iron: the rights of churches immediately subject to the Roman pontiff remaining intact.

Moreover, when the provostship of your church was vacant, we grant you free authority to assign it to a suitable person with the assent of the greater and sounder part of the chapter. If we have written to your devotion concerning its assignment, or concerning conferring another benefice of your church upon anyone, we do not wish you to be bound to carry out the apostolic mandate, unless the person for whom apostolic letters have been issued is honourable and worthy of the benefice. This provision concerning the future vacancy of your church is proposed . . . [Col. 1342A] let the assignment of a suitable person be reported to us in your letters, lest through ignorance of the facts we should be compelled to write to you again. And since by right and custom it is said to belong to the bishop of Poitiers for the time being to appoint one canon in the collegiate churches of clerics in the diocese of Poitiers, and likewise in the church of Daurac, by this present document we prohibit anyone, under pretext of appeal, from obstructing what belongs to you in this regard.

Moreover, since certain religious men who can scarcely suffice to govern one priory often seek two through blameworthy ambition and presume to retain them, we command your discretion to restrain this presumption, and, appeal being set aside, compel abbots, archpriests, and deans established throughout your diocese to receive priestly orders, if they are suitable. [Col. 1342B] Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our concession and prohibition or, by rash daring, to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of the blessed Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, on the third Ides of March.

CCXXII. Privilege for the monastery of the Valley of Saint John at Seitz. (Verona, March 19.)

[TRAELICH, *Sacred Diplomatic Records of the Duchy of Styria*, vol. II, p. 65.]

[Col. 1342C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the Carthusian brothers who are in the Valley of Saint John: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting for us readily to give assent to the just desires of petitioners and to fulfil by corresponding effect the vows that do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, heartily assenting to your just requests, we confirm by apostolic authority, and strengthen by the protection of this present document, the estate of Gunuwitz in the patriarchate of Aquileia, in which your cells are founded, together with its rights of use and appurtenances, granted to your order by our beloved sons, noblemen Otacher, margrave [Col. 1342D] of Styria, and Otacher, duke, his son, just as you possess it lawfully and peacefully. The boundaries of this estate, as is set out in the charter of that same margrave, are the mountain summits down to the valley, and on the other side the estate of the Church of Gurk.
