Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation or, by rash daring, oppose it. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of April.

CCXXIII. He receives the monastery of Saint Mary of Charity under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. (Verona, March 19.)

[HUGO, *Annals of the Sacred and Canonical Order of Prémontré*, vol. II, Documents, p. 96.]

[Col. 1343A]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons JOHN, abbot of Saint Mary of Charity, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life in perpetuity.

It is fitting that apostolic protection should be present for those choosing the religious life, lest the assault of any rash person either turn them aside from their purpose or, which God forbid, weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, [Col. 1343B] beloved sons in Christ, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of Saint Mary of Charity, situated outside the city of Rodrigo, in which you are devoted to divine service. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order recognized as established in that church according to God, the Rule of blessed Augustine, and the institution of the Premonstratensian brothers, shall there be observed inviolate for all time. Furthermore, whatever possessions or goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, God granting, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names:

[Col. 1343C] The place itself in which the aforesaid church is situated, with all its appurtenances and surrounding possessions; the church of Saint Leonard with its appurtenances; the possessions which it has at Caldelis; the possessions which it has at Gassapos; the possessions which it has at Eltis; the mills (*asenias*) which you have on the stream of Agada; and the houses which you have in the city of Rodrigo. Let no one presume to demand or extort tithes from you from your newly cultivated lands, which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the increase of your animals. You are also permitted [Col. 1343D] to receive into conversion clerics or laymen fleeing the world, who are free and unencumbered, and retain them without any opposition.

Furthermore, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, from leaving it without his abbot’s permission; and no one shall dare retain a departing brother without letters of the community certifying the matter. When a general interdict of the land is in force, you may celebrate the divine offices behind closed doors, with excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice. For chrism, holy oil, consecrations of churches, ordinations of clerics to be promoted to sacred orders, the installation of an abbot at his see, or any [Col. 1344A] other ecclesiastical sacraments, no one shall dare demand anything from you, whether under pretext of custom or in any other manner. But if anyone presumes to act against this, let him know that he will have a portion with Gehazi, whose deed he imitates by demanding a shameful gift (4 Kings 5). We also decree that the burial-place of that establishment shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have determined to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken remaining unimpaired.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, [Col. 1344B] diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the use and benefit of those for whose support and governance they were granted, the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop being preserved. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject to divine vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all [Col. 1344C] who preserve their rights for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of peace. Amen.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mary across the Tiber. I, Hubert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Albinus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. [Col. 1344D] I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, Theodinus, bishop of the see of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Arditio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Gratian, deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Soffredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata.

Given at Verona through the hands of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the third indiction, in the year 1184 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

CCXXIV. He receives the monastery of Romain under protection and confirms its immunity from tallages and from other new and unlawful exactions. (Verona, March 23.)

[*Memoirs and Documents of the Society of Roman Switzerland*, vol. III, p. 588.]

[Col. 1345A]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the prior and convent of the monastery of Romain: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The authority of our office urges us to concern ourselves with the condition of religious places and, with the Lord’s help, to provide beneficially for their peace and tranquillity in the future. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, heartily assenting to your just requests, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves your monastery, together with all that it now reasonably possesses or may hereafter acquire by just means, God granting, and strengthen it by the protection of this present document. We strictly prohibit archbishops, bishops, archdeacons, or any other ecclesiastical persons from presuming henceforth to extort from you or your priests such or any other new and unlawful exactions contrary to the statutes of the Lateran Council. [Col. 1345B] Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our protection and constitution or, by rash daring, to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God [Col. 1345C] and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, on the tenth day before the Kalends of April.

CCXXV. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Minias near Florence. (Verona, March.)

[*Annals of Camaldoli*, IV, 126.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ALBERT of Saint Minias and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life in perpetuity.

It is fitting that apostolic protection should be present for those choosing the religious life, lest the assault of any rash person either turn them away from their purpose or weaken, [Col. 1345D] which God forbid, the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the abbey of Saint Minias, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. First, indeed, we decree that the monastic order recognized as established in that place according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall there be observed inviolate for all time. Furthermore, whatever possessions or goods it now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, God granting, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you [Col. 1346A] and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify by their proper names:

The place itself in which the aforesaid church is situated, with all its adjacent lands and appurtenances; the church of Saint Nicholas with the adjoining parish, as you justly and without dispute possess it, namely from the stream of Corbulo as far as [lacuna] above the Arno; the church of Saint Peter near Ima, with its estate and appurtenances; [lacuna] of Musciano, with its appurtenances; [lacuna] the tithe-right [*decimatio*] [lacuna] which you have in [lacuna] of Intinnula [lacuna] and now peacefully possess; likewise that which you have in the parish church of Saint Peter [lacuna] in the territory of the parish church of Saint Mary of Pineta; the church of Saint Mary of Quinto, with its estate and appurtenances [Col. 1346B]; the tithe-right which you have in the parish church of Saint Martin of Sesto; the church of Saint Mary of Novule, with its estate and appurtenances; the tithe-right which you have throughout the whole parish district of Saint Martin of Corella, with its estate and all its tithe-rights and appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary of Albuino, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Donatus in the greater plain; the castle of Monte Acuto, with its church and appurtenances; the castle of Monte Alto, with its church, estate, and appurtenances; the patronage which you have in the church of Saint Andrew of Doccia; the holding of Campi; the tithe which you have in the parish district of Saint Stephen of Campi; the tithe which you have in the parish church of Empoli; the tithes of Mount Cross and Mount Fiesole; the church [Col. 1346C] of Saint Peter of Camilia, with its appurtenances; every tithe-right which you have on the hill of Saint Minias and in the parish church of Saint Reparata, just as hitherto you have held it canonically and now possess it without dispute.

You may also receive into conversion clerics and laymen [lacuna] who are free and unencumbered, and retain them without contradiction. When a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, you may celebrate the divine offices in a low voice, with doors closed, bells not rung, and excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded. We strengthen and confirm by apostolic authority for you the ancient and reasonable customs of your church observed down to the present time, and the tithes which you have peacefully possessed for forty years until now [Col. 1346D]. We further grant that the burial-place of that same house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have resolved to be buried there, provided that they are not excommunicated or under interdict, while nevertheless preserving the right of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, or to take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be kept whole, for the complete benefit of the uses for which they were granted, namely the governance and support of those concerned, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc. [Col. 1347A]

**HELP US, O GOD OF OUR SALVATION.**

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theodorus, bishop of the see of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Mark. I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Callixtus. I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of the title of the Twelve Apostles. I, Ardicio, cardinal-deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Gratian, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian [Col. 1347B]. I, Soffredus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Albinus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary Nova.

Given at Verona through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, [lacuna] March, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1184, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Pope Lucius III.

## CCXXVI. Privilege for the Chapter of Pistoia.  
*(Verona, 4 April.)*

[ZACHARIA, *Anecdota medii aevi*, 235.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons [Col. 1347C], Nivaldus, provost of the Church of Pistoia, and his brethren, both present and future, to be canonically appointed, for ever.

A desire which is shown to concern the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls must, with God as its author, be fulfilled without any delay. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, Urban, Eugenius, and Alexander, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of Saint Peter and of ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present document, the hospital-house of Umbroncello, which your predecessors are known to have built through their efforts and at their expense. [Col. 1347D] We decree that whatever possessions and goods the said house now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with God’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to it. We have judged that the following should be expressly set down by their proper names:

Of the tithes given to you by the people, a tenth share; and the tithes of your own labours, as has unanimously been ordained by those same predecessors of yours. Moreover, we grant a privilege of the same tenor to the other hospitals situated throughout your bishopric: namely, that built near the village of Quarrata; that near the town of Capraria; that in the meadow called [Col. 1348A] Bishop’s Meadow; and that beside the place called Brandelian Cross; the hospital of Doccio, which was granted to you by its founder, named Esnellus, through a public charter; and also that at Brisceto, built through the efforts and at the expense of your predecessors. We decree that this latter shall be subject in perpetuity to your aforesaid hospice of Umbroncello, as was ordained by our aforementioned predecessor.

Since these hospital-houses stand outside cities, we establish by the decree of this privilege that no one may presume, within one stadium of them, to seize anyone, plunder, or make hostile disturbance. We have entrusted all their regulations and arrangements to you and your successors, following the example of the aforesaid Pope Alexander, so that, by the common will of those among you who are more religious, and with the counsel also of the brethren of the Valley of Umbronia having been taken, and likewise with the consent of your bishop, if he is Catholic, [Col. 1348B] governors may be appointed over those houses who will undertake to care for them according to God’s will and diligently minister to the poor who come there.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb those houses, seize anyone in them, take away or diminish the possessions subject to them, or harass them with reckless vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole, to benefit the uses for whose support they have been granted and the salvation of those who have made offerings, saving the authority of the Apostolic See [Col. 1348C]. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theodinus, bishop of the see of Porto and Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Mark. I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Mary across the Tiber and of Callixtus. I, Umbertus, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. [Col. 1348D] I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of the title of the Twelve Apostles. I, Albinus, priest-cardinal of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Melior, priest-cardinal of Saints John, Paul, and Pamachius. I, Arditio, cardinal-deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Gratian, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Soffredus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata.

Given at Verona through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second Nones of April [4 April], in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1185, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Pope Lucius III.

## CCXXVII. He receives under protection the monastery of the Scots of Saint James at Regensburg and confirms its possessions and privileges.  
*(Verona, 10 April.)*

[RIED, *Codex diplomaticus Ratisbonensis*, II, 267.]

[Col. 1349A]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Gregory, abbot of the monastery of Saint James at Regensburg, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

Those choosing the religious life ought to have apostolic protection at hand, lest perhaps an assault of any rashness either recall them from their purpose or, which God forbid, weaken the strength of holy religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, Eugenius, Adrian, and Alexander, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of Saint Peter and of ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present document, the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service. [Col. 1349B] First, we decree that the monastic order which is known to have been established in that place according to God and the Rule of Saint Benedict shall be observed there inviolate for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with God’s help, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Upon the death of you, who are now abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it through any device of deceit or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall judge to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict.

Furthermore, if pilgrims and newly arriving guests are not subject by parish right to any church of Regensburg, and die while staying with you, then, as has been maintained by ancient custom in your church, you may, notwithstanding any opposition, give them ecclesiastical burial if they have freely wished to be buried there. Since certain churches have received their order from you and are subject to [Col. 1349D] your governance, we decree, lest the discipline of regular observance decay in them, that, as is customary, the leading persons of those churches shall come to your monastery once every year, where they shall humbly receive from you and observe both correction for their transgressions and the ordinances of the order.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be kept whole, for the complete benefit of the uses for which they were granted, namely the governance and support of those concerned, saving the canonical right of the bishop of Regensburg. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

[Col. 1350A] I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Then follows the subscription of ten cardinals.

Given at Verona through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth Ides of April [10 April], in the fourth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1185, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Pope Lucius III.

## CCXXVIII. Bull for the Chapter of Saint Martin at Tours.  
*(Verona, 17 April.)*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the dean, treasurer, and chapter of Saint Martin of Tours: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more especially your church belongs by right to Saint Peter [Col. 1350B] and has obtained from our predecessors a greater prerogative of liberty, the more abundantly do we sympathize with its need, and the more attentively ought—and desire—we to provide for its advantages and peace. Accordingly, we confirm by apostolic authority the renunciation of the commune or conspiracy, by whatever name it may be called, which we annulled with the counsel of the brethren and which was received by our venerable brother W., archbishop of Reims, cardinal of Saint Sabina, legate of the Apostolic See, and by our beloved son the abbot of Marmoutier, to whom this had been entrusted by us. Under threat of anathema, we forbid anyone henceforth to seek it under any pretext.

Let no person whatsoever, therefore, be permitted to infringe this document [Col. 1350C] of our confirmation and prohibition, or rashly to oppose it. If anyone shall presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, on the fifteenth Kalends of May [17 April].

## CCXXIX. Foundation of the monastery of Trutenhusen, of the Order of Saint Augustine in the diocese of Strasbourg; or rather confirmation of that foundation.  
*(Verona, 20 April.)*

[Gallia Christiana nova, V, *Instrumenta*, p. 486.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, Herrad, abbess, and the sisters [Col. 1350D] in the monastery of Hohenburg, both present and future, professing the regular life: apostolic blessing and the joy of everlasting salvation.

With fatherly love we make known to all the faithful of the whole Church that it has been reported to us by a truthful statement that Duke Frederick, father of Emperor Frederick, disturbed the church called Hohenburg, founded in honour of Saint Mary, Mother of God, in which rests the body of Saint Odilia the virgin, through indiscriminate seizure of its property; and that he left it almost destroyed until the time of his son, Emperor Frederick. Emperor Frederick himself, moved by divine grace, grieved deeply over his father’s wretched offence and, desiring to reconcile to himself the favour of the eternal King, laboured to restore the aforesaid church upon the counsel of spiritual persons. As he learned from them, he placed over that church a religious and suitable person named Rilint.

When she happily assumed the governance of the church, she diligently rebuilt what had been destroyed for the love of God and vigorously planted what had been laid waste. With the assistance and counsel of Burchard, bishop of Strasbourg, and other spiritual persons, she prudently and honourably reformed that church to the honour of God, and fully established there all the religious observance of the divine law and the rigor of canonical discipline according to the Rule of Saint Augustine. Her successor, our beloved daughter in Christ, Abbess Herrad, faithfully followed this standard of endeavour in every good work; among the other useful works to which she devoted attention [Col. 1351B], she, together with her convent and with Gunther of Vinbege, purchased the estate at Trutenhusen from certain ministerials of that abbey. She conveyed it upon the high altar at Hohenburg on the condition that, through her efforts, a provostship of regular canons should be founded there to the honour of God and of the abbey of Hohenburg. They were to be established and remain according to the Rule of Saint Augustine and the custom of the church of Marbach.

With the favour and counsel of our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, ever august emperor of the Romans, and with the consent of the ministerials of that church, and the approval also of Peter, bishop of Tusculum, of good memory, then legate of the Apostolic See, and of Henry, bishop of Strasbourg, she ordained and built there first a chapel in honour of God and in memory of the Blessed Mary ever Virgin, and an estate with the other buildings, until a larger church—that is, a monastery—might be constructed there in memory of Saint Nicholas, together with cloister buildings: namely, a hospital for the poor, a lodging-house for arriving guests, and the other buildings necessary for a church. In it twelve canons are to be installed, with a suitable provost of the same order. Living under regular profession, they shall devoutly obey in the fear of God the abbesses and the whole community of the abbey of Hohenburg in spiritual and temporal matters, as the abbess and the necessity of the abbey may require; nor shall they through any rash presumption haughtily trouble the church of Hohenburg. [Col. 1351D]

For these canons, at the aforesaid church of Trutenhusen, founded under the arrangement described above, she decreed, with the assent already mentioned, to give the revenues of two weekly prebends, to be distributed not for private use but for the common benefit: namely, two cartloads of wine; two talents of Strasbourg denarii; twenty-eight *malders* of winter grain; fourteen *malders* of barley; and the benefices situated in Lower Ehenheim and Rodesheim belonging to the same prebends; and the tithe of the Salian land at Sunthusen, together with the tithes of the Salian land at Egensheim belonging to those same prebends; and whatever shall be offered into the hands of the provost or his vicars at Hohenburg. [Col. 1352A]

Furthermore, for their use she has now granted at Gokkeswilre thirty-two and a half arable *jugera*, and two vineyard *jugera* with trees, two gardens, and an estate; at Bercheim she granted them fourteen *jugera* and one estate; likewise, at Heilingenstein, seven vineyard *jugera*. All these do not belong to the prebends. In addition, she granted them in its entirety the allod of Trutenhusen itself.

It was likewise established that every provost at Trutenhusen, whenever he wishes, shall visit the church of Hohenburg and celebrate the solemnities of the Mass according to the order of that church; and that he shall always appoint at Hohenburg two religious and suitable weekly-serving canons from among his own canons. If the aforesaid priests should at any time have to be replaced, the provost shall freely recall them to the cloister, without any opposition from the abbess, and shall take care to appoint other suitable men, who, without departing from the mountain without the abbess’s permission, shall not refuse to celebrate the divine offices without any burden according to the custom of the church of Hohenburg. [Col. 1352B]

Moreover, on the Purification of Saint Mary, Palm Sunday, Maundy Thursday, the Nativity and the Beheading of Saint John the Baptist, the Assumption of Saint Mary, the feast of Saint Michael, and All Saints, he shall come annually to the monastery of Hohenburg to celebrate the solemn Mass, unless an unavoidable cause prevents him. Also, on the feast of Saint Odilia, at the dedication of her chapel, and at the Nativity of the Lord, he shall celebrate the earlier daytime Mass.

If the provost and his canons neglect these decrees of the privilege and disturb the church of Hohenburg with an unreasonable burden, the abbess and convent shall withdraw the prebends and the benefices belonging to the prebends, and shall procure elsewhere, for themselves, such peaceful and religious priests as they wish. Those canons, however, shall no longer dare to celebrate on Mount Hohenburg the offices at the solemnities of Mass which had previously been granted to them, unless by permission of the abbess and convent, just as outsiders may not do so. [Col. 1352C]

Likewise, if the abbot of Stivagium and his canons attack the church of Hohenburg contentiously through unjust opposition, and do not observe, in meek obedience, the ordinances of their privilege given from the hand of the abbess of Hohenburg, the place of Gorgonius, which is the prebend of one weekly-serving canon, with all its appurtenances—which every abbot of Stivagium ought to receive from the abbess of Hohenburg—and the other benefices received from Hohenburg shall be withdrawn from them. Other suitable priests shall be chosen elsewhere at the will of the abbess and convent; and they themselves shall no longer dare, like outsiders, to celebrate the solemnities of Mass on Mount Hohenburg unless by permission of the abbess. [Col. 1352D]

It was also decreed by unanimous counsel and consent that, whenever a provost at Trutenhusen departs this present life or is transferred, the brethren living there shall elect a suitable and religious person of their order. The person so elected shall, on his first arrival, receive freely and without any opposition, by the book, investiture of the provostship from the hand of the abbess of Hohenburg. It was further added that the church at Trutenhusen shall be defended under the patronage of the advocate of Hohenburg, and that every secular cause to be heard there shall be examined in the court of that advocate.

Now, therefore, because our aforesaid daughter Herrad, venerable abbess, has asked that these pious and religious ordinances be confirmed by our protection and strengthened by apostolic protection, we graciously concur with her request. We confirm the aforesaid constitution by apostolic authority, receive that place under the protection of Saint Peter and of ourselves, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s help, shall remain secure and unimpaired to the brethren and their successors. [Col. 1353B]

They may also receive into conversion persons free and unencumbered who flee from the world, and retain them without any opposition. Moreover, we prohibit any canon, after making profession in that place, from leaving it without permission of his provost; and no one may dare to retain a person who has left without a written assurance from the community. When a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, they may celebrate the divine offices in a low voice, with doors closed, bells not rung, and excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded. Desiring with fatherly care to provide for the peace and tranquillity of the brethren, we prohibit by apostolic authority anyone from committing violence, robbery, or theft, setting fire, seizing, or killing a person within the enclosures of their places or granges. We further decree that the burial-place of that house shall be free both for the brethren and for the household, pilgrims, or guests who die there, unless they happen to be excommunicated or under interdict. [Col. 1353C]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the complete benefit of the uses for which they were granted, namely the governance and support of those concerned, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this document of our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it, and after a second or third warning does not amend the offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of rank and office; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most holy body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. [Col. 1354A] But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

Given at Verona through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth Kalends of May [20 April], in the fourth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation **1851** [an evident chronological error for 1185], in the fourth year of the pontificate of Pope Lucius III.

## CCXXX. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary of Holm Cultram.  
*(Verona, April–May.)*

*Monasticon Anglicanum*, III.

[Col. 1354B]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Everard, abbot of the monastery of Saint Mary of Holm Cultram, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

Those choosing the religious life ought to have apostolic protection at hand, lest perhaps an assault of any rashness either recall them from their purpose or, which God forbid, weaken the strength of holy religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests, and receive under the protection of Saint Peter and of ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present document, the aforesaid monastery of Saint Mary of Holm Cultram, in which you are devoted to divine service. [Col. 1354C] First, we decree that the monastic order known to have been established in that place according to God, the Rule of Saint Benedict, and the Cistercian institution shall be observed there inviolate for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s help, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have judged that the following should be expressly set down by their proper names:

[Col. 1354D] By the gift of the illustrious King Henry of England, the whole island of Holme, in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with all its appurtenances and all liberties granted to you by that illustrious king and confirmed by his charter; the Old Grange with all its appurtenances; the grange of Ternis with all its appurtenances; the grange of Senile with all its appurtenances; the grange of Rabi, with all, etc.; the grange of Arlosk, with all, etc.; and everything which you have within the island of Holme by its rightful boundaries, as it was forested in the time of the elder King Henry and Ranulf, earl of Chester.

Outside the island of Holme, by gift of Cospatric son of Orm and Thomas son of Cospatric, the land and grange of Flemingeby, with all [Col. 1355A] their appurtenances, within their rightful boundaries, as is contained in their charters. Also, by gift of the same Cospatric, the land of Keltone with all its easements, as is contained in his charter; further, the liberties of the same land by gift of Count William and Countess Cecilia of Aumale; and, by gift of the same count and countess, one forge at Winnefel with all its necessaries, as is contained in their charters. By gift of Waltheof son of Gamel, the land of Kirkebythore with all its appurtenances; also the grange and land in Galloway called Kirkewinni, with all its appurtenances, within its boundaries as they are clearly set forth in the charter of Roland son of Hratrid [lacuna]; also one salt-pan, outside those same boundaries, in Lotchchidale [lacuna], with its necessaries [Col. 1355B]; and pasture for pigs free from pannage throughout all woods within the lordship of that same Roland, and woodland easements in Preston and Lotch [lacuna], and paths and port easements. All these are as contained in the charter of Roland himself.

Likewise, in Ireland, whatever Count Richard, Hugh de Lacy, and other nobles have bestowed upon you and your house out of pious regard, and fortified by their charters, we confirm to you nonetheless by apostolic authority.

We also forbid anyone to give personally, or alienate in another manner, lands or any benefice granted to your church without the consent of the whole chapter, or of its greater and sounder part. If any gifts or alienations are made otherwise than as has been stated, [Col. 1355C] we declare them void.

Moreover, we hold valid the ancient, reasonable, and regular customs of your monastery observed hitherto, and decree that they shall remain unimpaired in future times. No one may presume to extort tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, from the increase of your animals, or from your fisheries, wherever they may be, whether in salt waters or rivers. You may also receive into conversion clerics or laymen fleeing from the world, who are free and unencumbered, and retain them in your monastery without any opposition.

Moreover, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in your house, from leaving it without the permission of his abbot; and no one may dare to retain one who has left without a written assurance from the community. We also prohibit by apostolic authority anyone from presuming to burden your monastery with new exactions. Desiring with fatherly care to provide for your peace and tranquillity, we prohibit by apostolic authority anyone from committing violence, robbery, or theft, setting fire, seizing, or killing a person in any manner within the precinct of your monastery and the enclosures of your places or granges. [Col. 1355D]

Furthermore, we add that no brother or lay brother bound by the profession of your house shall, without the consent and permission of the abbot and the greater part of your chapter, stand surety for anyone or borrow money from anyone beyond the sum fixed by the prudent judgment of the chapter for the manifest benefit of your house. If he should nevertheless presume to do so, the convent, without whose permission and consent he had undertaken this, shall not be bound in any way to answer for those debts. [Col. 1356A]

Furthermore, it shall be lawful for you, in your lawsuits, to produce suitable brethren as witnesses and, through their testimony, if it is right, both to repel violence and to vindicate justice. For holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, the ordination of monks who are to be promoted to sacred orders, the conducting of an abbot to his see, or any other sacraments, no one may dare to demand anything from you, whether under the pretext of custom or in any other way. [Col. 1356B]

We also decree that no bishop or other person, secular or of another order, shall ever impede the regular and canonical election of your abbot, nor in any way interfere in the deposition of the incumbent, contrary to the statutes of the Cistercian Order and the authority of your privileges. Moreover, if the bishop in whose parish your house has been founded, having been asked three times with the humility and devotion proper to the matter, should perhaps refuse to bless your abbot once he has been appointed, that abbot, if he is a priest, may bless his own novices and exercise the other functions belonging to that office, until that bishop reflects upon his harshness and does not refuse to bless the abbot who is to be blessed. [Col. 1356C]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the complete benefit of the uses for which they were granted, namely the governance and support of those concerned, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

Given, etc., 8 May, in the year of the Lord 1185, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Pope Lucius III.

## CCXXXI. He informs [Hartwig II], archbishop of Hamburg, that he has postponed summoning the disobedient bishops of Denmark, Sweden, and Norway because of the disturbed condition of those kingdoms.  
*(Verona, 4 May.)*

[LAPPENBERG, *Hamburgische Urkunden*, I, 238.]

[Col. 1356D]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother, the archbishop of Bremen: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although the messenger whom you had left at the Apostolic See, to urge us to summon the bishops established throughout Denmark, Sweden, and Norway to answer concerning the obedience which they are said to have withdrawn from your church, pressed very strongly, it did not seem good to us or to our brethren that, amid so great a disturbance as is now said to exist in the aforesaid kingdoms, and during the newness of [the beginning of] your office, we ought to satisfy his insistence. [Col. 1357A]

You, therefore, considering that what is postponed is not taken away, must not ascribe our deferral of hearing this petition to negligence or to any lesser affection which we have toward you; rather, await with us a more favourable opportunity, since, at the appropriate time, with God’s help, we shall gladly attend to your advantage and honour.

Given at Verona, on the fourth Nones of May [4 May].

## CCXXXII. Privileges for the monastery of Saints Peter and Vitus of Calavena.  
*(Verona, 13 June.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 803.]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Simeon, abbot of the monastery of Saints Peter and Vitus of Calavena, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, for ever. [Col. 1357B]

A pious petition, etc., we fortify. First, we decree that the monastic order known to have been established in that monastery according to God and the Rule of Saint Benedict shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s help, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors [Col. 1357C]. Among these we have judged that the following should be expressly set down by their proper names.

The very place in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with all its appurtenances; the chapel of Saint Faustinus in the castle of Verona; the chapel of Saint Ambrose in the court of Mezzane, together with the stream, the mills, and all its other appurtenances; and the chapel of Saint Nicholas at Colonia, with all its appurtenances; the chapel of Saint Andrew situated at Illasio, with all its appurtenances; the chapel of Saint Vitalis situated at Cuculo, with all its appurtenances; the estate of Coculo with its district and other appurtenances. Whatever right and property you possess in the estates of Treniaco, Marcemici, Centuli, Casali, and [Col. 1357D] Custnani; the court of Cosparini, with tithes and its other appurtenances; and whatever right and property you possess in the courts of Illasio, Coloniola, Calderii, Porcili, Caput Alponis, Saint John of Adrovia, Mezzana, Trezzolani, Colonia, and Cavaloni; the church of Saint Mary on the Island of Verona; the tithes of Cosparini, Sorceti, and Cesolini; the tithes of Calderii; and the tithes of the fifteen holdings of Casalvini in Treniaco, Caseri, and Cusnani; the tithes of Coculi and of Cerredi; and, moreover, the tithes of the entire allod of your monastery mentioned above. Just as you canonically possess these tithes, we confirm them to you and to your monastery by apostolic authority.

Moreover, let no one presume to demand or extort from you tithes of your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or of the produce of your animals; and it shall be lawful for you to receive into conversion clerics and laymen fleeing the world, free and unbound, and to retain them without any opposition. Furthermore, we forbid any one of your brethren, after making profession in that place, to depart from it without his abbot’s permission, except for the sake of a stricter religious life; and let no one dare retain a departing brother without letters of the community attesting the matter. When, however, a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, it shall be lawful for you, with doors shut, bells not rung, excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded, and in a subdued voice, to celebrate the divine offices. Let no cleric presume to demand or receive tithes from you from your own labour or revenues. [Col. 1358A]

We also confirm by apostolic authority the agreement made between you and the parish of Cavalena concerning certain tithes, just as it has been mutually accepted and is contained in public documents. Moreover, we decree that the burial-place of that monastery shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last wishes of those who resolve to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while preserving nevertheless the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. Upon the death of yourself, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed there by any cunning device of usurpation or by force, save one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Saint Benedict, provide to be elected. [Col. 1358B–C]

We therefore decree, etc., saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theodinus, bishop of the See of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary in Trastevere. I, Pandulphus, cardinal priest of the title of the Twelve Apostles. I, Albinus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Melior, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul of Pammachius. [Col. 1358D] I, Adelard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Soffredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Roland, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere. I, Pandulphus, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Ides of June, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1185, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Lucius III, pope.

## CCXXXIII. He confirms the agreement made between [John], bishop of Grenoble, and [Hugh], duke of Burgundy. (Verona, June 13.)

*[Histoire du Dauphiné, I, Proofs, 182.]*

[Col. 1359A]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother, the bishop of Grenoble: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has been reported to us on your behalf that, when the nobleman the Duke of Burgundy had raised a dispute against you concerning the land of Plana, certain mills, and many other matters, an amicable agreement was at last reached between you concerning all these things, which is said to have been strengthened by the solemnity of an oath and by a public document. Therefore, in order that it may henceforth possess unshaken validity, we confirm by apostolic authority that same agreement, as it was made and accepted with the consent of the parties and as it is contained in a public document; and we strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. [Col. 1359B]

Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, on the Ides of June.

## CCXXXIV. He confirms certain revenues for the weekly ministers of the Church of Épinal. (Verona, June 18.)

*[D. Calmet, History of Lorraine, II, Proofs, p. 389.]*

[Col. 1359C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons STEPHEN, BALDAM, DOMINIC, and GARIN, weekly ministers of the Church of Épinal: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners, and bring to effect the requests that do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously concurring in your just petitions, we confirm to you four and to your successors, by apostolic authority, and strengthen by the protection of this present writing, the revenues assigned canonically and in full to support you by our beloved daughter in Christ, the abbess of Épinal, and confirmed by Peter, bishop of Toul, just as you possess them lawfully and peacefully, [Col. 1359D] and as they are contained in the authentic documents of the late bishops Stephen and Peter, of good memory, and of the abbess herself.

Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of July [18 June].

## CCXXXV. Privilege for the convent of nuns at Épinal. (Verona, June 19.)

*[Ibid.]*

[Col. 1360A]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, SIBYLLA, abbess, and the convent of Épinal: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Those provisions established by the reasoned care of pontiffs for the observance of divine worship ought not to be changed by any presumption; and, that they may have greater firmness, they should be confirmed by apostolic protection. Therefore, assenting to your just petitions, we confirm by apostolic authority the ordinance which Stephen, bishop of Metz, of good memory, is said to have made and [Col. 1360B] confirmed by his own written instrument—namely, that in your church four weekly ministers, of mature age and upright conduct, shall continually serve in their turns. By these present letters we establish that what was long ago arranged by prudent deliberation concerning their prebends, and has hitherto been observed, shall be observed inviolably.

Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation and ordinance, or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of July [19 June].

## CCXXXVI. Privilege concerning the liberty of the borough of Saint-Remi granted by the archbishop: that its inhabitants are not to be seized at Reims, and concerning markets. (Verona, July 5.)

*[Varin, Administrative Archives of Reims, I, I, 404.]*

[Col. 1360C]

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons SIMON, abbot, and the convent of Saint-Remi: greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the tenor of the authentic document [Note: [Col. 1359] This charter, dated 1182, is found in cartulary B of Saint-Remi, p. 57. It contains nothing not reproduced by the bull of Lucius III.] of our venerable brother W., archbishop of Reims, cardinal of Saint Sabina and legate of the Apostolic See, it has become known to us that he, inspired by the Lord and providing for your tranquility and peace and that of all your people in the future, confirmed by his own written instrument your liberties and customs, your dues [Col. 1360D] as well, the *ban* [right of command], justice, the sextellarium, the markets of Friday and Sunday, ovens and mills, and the other things which you have hitherto possessed. He established that your men, or others living in your borough, when going to or returning from Reims for legal causes or any other business, shall enjoy uninterrupted security; and neither they nor their goods are to be seized or detained by his provosts or officials, or by any other persons, so long as they are willing to render justice under your jurisdiction, unless perhaps they have been caught in a present offence.

Accordingly, holding the act of the same archbishop valid, we confirm by apostolic authority for your devotion the aforesaid liberty and the other things reasonably granted you by that [Col. 1361A] archbishop’s provision, as they are more fully contained in the authentic document of the archbishop himself.

We therefore decree, etc.

Given at Verona, on the third day before the Nones of July [5 July].

## CCXXXVII. He approves a judgment issued for the monastery of Saint Saviour by the bishop of Torcello and the prior of Charity, apostolic delegates. (Verona, July 13.)

*[Cornelius, Venetian Church, vol. XIV, p. 111.]*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons G., prior, and the canons of Saint Saviour of Venice: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1361B] Matters concluded by judgment or agreement ought to remain firm and inviolate; and, lest in the course of time they be altered through anyone’s malice, they ought to be strengthened by letters [lacuna] and by our protection. Since, however, a dispute had for some time been conducted between you and Jo. Premarino, parish priest of Saint Bartholomew, concerning certain parishioners, at length our venerable brother, the bishop of Torcello [lacuna], and our beloved son [lacuna], prior of Saint Mary of Charity, to whom this case had been committed by apostolic mandate, having heard the arguments and allegations put forward on both sides, brought the matter to a concluded judgment. Therefore we confirm by apostolic authority that same judgment, as it was reasonably issued, and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing.

[Col. 1361C] Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of the blessed Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, on the third day before the Ides of July [13 July].

## CCXXXVIII. He confirms the goods and privileges of the monastery of Admont, and adds new provisions concerning the election of abbesses and the governance of other monasteries. (Verona, July 22.)

*[Pez, Treasury, III, III, 671.]*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ISENRIC, abbot of the monastery of Saint Blaise called Admont, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

The authority of our office admonishes and invites us to be zealous for the condition of churches, and, with the Lord’s assistance, to provide beneficially for their repose and tranquility. For it is judged worthy and consonant with propriety that we who, by the Lord’s ordering, have been appointed to their governance should protect them from the wickedness of evil men and fortify them by the patronage of blessed Peter and the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to the just petitions of our venerable brother Albert, your archbishop, and to your own; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors Paschal, Innocent, Lucius, and Alexander, Roman pontiffs of good memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid monastery [Col. 1362A] in which you are devoted to divine service. We establish that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now lawfully and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, with the Lord’s favour, through the grant of pontiffs, the largesse of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and inviolate to you and your successors. Of these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

[Col. 1362B] *(Here the goods are enumerated as in the bull of Alexander III, issued 4 February 1170 [Note: [Col. 1361D] See volume CC of the Patrologia].)*

[lacuna] Nor shall the bishop, the abbot himself, or any person have power to grant the goods of the same monastery to anyone as a fief or benefice, or to alienate them in any other manner. Moreover, we judge the burial-place of that institution to be free, so that no one may oppose the last wishes of those who desire to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while preserving the right of the mother church. No opposition by any bishop, abbot, or provost shall prevent you from receiving for conversion laymen or secular clerics, or persons coming to you from other monasteries through a desire for a stricter life or for another certain and reasonable cause. We also forbid any brother, after making [Col. 1362C] profession, to depart from the same cloister without the permission of the abbot and the entire community; and let no one dare retain a departing brother without letters of the community attesting the matter.

Moreover, let no one presume to demand tithes from you of your newly cleared lands cultivated by your own hands or at your own expense, or of the produce of your animals. Nor shall anyone be permitted to impose upon the monastery forced labour-services or other new exactions contrary to monastic peace and religious life. Whatever our most beloved son Frederick, Augustus, emperor of the Romans, granted you by force of an imperial edict and confirmed by privilege, we likewise confirm by apostolic authority. In parish churches or chapels which you hold, it shall be lawful for you to elect priests [Col. 1362D] and present them to the bishop; if they are suitable, the bishop shall commit the care of souls to them, so that they shall answer to the bishop concerning the care of the people, but to you concerning temporal matters.

Furthermore, by apostolic authority we establish that, in the convents of nuns known to be entrusted to your governance, upon the death of abbesses another shall be elected jointly by the sisters with the counsel and assent of the abbot and brethren who provide them with necessities; or, once the election has been held, it shall be presented to the abbot, so that with his assent and support it may thereafter be presented to the bishops in whose dioceses they reside, for confirmation or rejection. But if the nuns do not make the election with the counsel and assent of the abbot and brethren who are to provide their necessities, or if the election once held is not then presented to your abbot, no bishop may bless persons elected without that presentation; they shall promise obedience and subjection to your abbot. [Col. 1363A] In addition, by this present decree we enact that you shall not be compelled to undertake the perpetual governance or administration of any monastery unless you have full power to order and govern that monastery in accordance with the statutes of your order. Upon the death of yourself, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed there by any cunning device of usurpation or by force, save one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of them, shall, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict, provide to be elected.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved undiminished and whole, for the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted, and beneficial in every way, saving the canonical reverence due to the Archbishop of Salzburg. Yet he shall by no means be permitted to impose upon it any vexation or custom harmful to the peace of regular religious. [Col. 1363B] If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this page of our constitution, and, having been warned a second and third time, does not correct this presumption by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there rest the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen. [Col. 1363C]

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina and archbishop of the See of Mainz, have subscribed. I, Theodwinus, bishop of the See of Porto and Saint Rufina, have subscribed. I, Heinrich, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark, have subscribed. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary in Trastevere, have subscribed. I, Hubert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence, have subscribed. I, Pandulfus, cardinal priest of the title of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. [Col. 1363D] I, Albinus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Adelard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Arditio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore, have subscribed. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Sofredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Roland, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Radulf, of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

[Col. 1364A] Given at Verona through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of August [22 July], in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1185, and in the fifth [fourth] year of the pontificate of Lord Lucius III, pope.

## CCXXXIX. He notifies the clerics of Rodigo that he has delegated to the bishop of Padua the case of a new church built by them to the prejudice of the church of Saint John the Baptist of Costa, subject to the monastery of Saint Cyprian of Murano. (Verona, July 26.)

*[Cornelii, Venetian Church, vol. X, part IV, p. 204.]*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the clerics of Rodigo: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1364C] From the report of our beloved son, the abbot of Saint Benedict on the Po, together with our beloved son, the prior of Saint Cyprian of Venice, we have learned that, after eighteen years had already elapsed since they had, with the permission of V., formerly bishop of Adria, of good memory, built a baptismal church in honour of Saint John in the village called Costa, you began in the same village to build a new church to the detriment of the old one, after an appeal to the Apostolic See had been entered and a notice of new work given. Therefore, committing the case to our venerable brother, the bishop of Padua, we command by apostolic letters that, when summoned to appear before him on this matter, you shall come to his presence and, without appeal, accept and firmly observe what he shall judge between you. [Col. 1364D]

Given at Verona, on the seventh day before the Kalends of August [26 July].

## CCXL. Privilege for the brethren of the Order of Saint John of Jerusalem. (Verona, August 22.)

*[Bosio, History of the Militia of Saint John, I, 66.]*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons R., master, and the brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more diligently, through the grace of God, you labour in service to the poor and relief of the sick, and daily advance in works of piety, stretching yourselves toward what lies before and forgetting what lies behind, the more sincerely we love your religious order and ought and desire more readily to hear your petitions that accord with law [Col. 1365A] and are consonant with piety; so that you may devote yourselves the more faithfully to observing your Rule, in proportion as you know it to be strengthened by the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your petitions and confirm by apostolic authority the Rule which your master Raymond, of pious memory, beneficially established by the common counsel and will of the chapter, and which, as we have learned, our predecessor Pope Eugenius, of happy memory, confirmed. We indeed have confidence through Christ toward God that, just as the Rule of blessed Augustine has been granted to regular canons unto salvation, so, by keeping your own Rule, you will attain the prize of eternal blessedness.

Furthermore, we approve the remedies prudently established for the care of the sick—namely, that there shall always be four physicians and an equal number of surgeons in the house of the Hospital, at whose direction those things necessary for the sick in food or other matters shall be supplied—and the many other provisions which you have beneficially ordained by committing them to writing. Under threat of anathema, we forbid their revocation by anyone, unless they should be changed by improvement. [Col. 1365B]

Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation and prohibition or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. [Col. 1365C]

I, Lucius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Theodoninus, cardinal bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina, have subscribed. I, Henry, cardinal bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Theobald, cardinal bishop of Ostia and Velletri, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark, have subscribed. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary in Trastevere, of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Pandulphus, cardinal priest of the Basilica of the Twelve [Col. 1365D] Apostles, have subscribed. I, Albinus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Melior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Adelard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore, have subscribed. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Gofredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Roland, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. [Col. 1366A] I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Rainerius, cardinal deacon of Saint George in Velabro, have subscribed.

Given at Verona through the hands of Albert, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of September [22 August], in the fourth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1185, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

## CCXLI. Privilege for the monastery of Burton. (Verona, September 3.)

*[Monasticon Anglicanum, vol. I, p. 270.]*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons RICHARD, abbot of the monastery of Burton, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

A pious request ought to be fulfilled in accordance with the petitioner’s desire, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth praiseworthily and the benefit requested may without doubt acquire force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery of Burton, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. First, we establish that the monastic order known to be instituted in that monastery according to the Lord and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall be observed there inviolably for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that monastery now lawfully and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, with the Lord’s favour, through the grant of pontiffs, the largesse of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and inviolate to you and your successors. Of these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: [Col. 1366B–C]

The place itself in which the monastery is situated, with all its appurtenances; the vill of Burton with its churches and all appurtenances; the vill of Branston; Sobenhal; the lands of Tatenhill, Horniglawe, Straton, Withmere, and Ansedelega; the vill of Wineshult, Bersicote, and Lichenhale; the vill of Stapenhulle, Appelby, Adulfestre, and Caldewell; [Col. 1366D] the land of Wulfricheston; the vill of Derlaheston with all its appurtenances; the vill of Bromlega with its church and all its appurtenances; and the vill of Felda and the vill of Lega, with their church and all their appurtenances, from the gift of Wulfric Spott, founder of your church.

From the gift of William, king of England, of good memory: the vill of Offra with its church and all its appurtenances; the vill of Little Offra with its chapel; Findernam with its chapel; Pothlac with its chapel; the vill of Wilentona with its church; the church of Saint Mary of Derbeya with two mills and land in the same vill; and the land of Hanofra. Likewise from the gift of the aforesaid Wulfric Spott: Plum, with its church and all its appurtenances; Acofram with its chapel; Cathesturne and the chapel of Blora with their [Col. 1367A] appurtenances; the chapel of Grendona with its appurtenances; the chapel of Calfdona; the chapel of Scona with the whole tithe; the tithe of Lintona, from that land belonging to the fee of Caldewella, with the whole tithe; likewise the entire tithe of Truelga; the tithe of Molidene; the tithe of Waterfale, from the part called Haselbache, together with a third sheaf from the other part; the land which you possess in Staffordia; the tithe of Neutuna; the land of Hamtona; the church of Stapehull with all its appurtenances, namely the tithe of Drachelawe with its chapel; the chapel of Hescote with the whole tithe; the chapel of Nova Aula with the whole tithe; and the entire tithe of Stantona.

Moreover, let no one presume to extort tithes from you of your newly cleared lands cultivated by your own hands or at your own expense, or of the produce of your animals. It shall also be lawful for you to receive into conversion clerics or laymen fleeing the world, free and absolved, and retain them without any opposition. Furthermore, we forbid any of your brethren, after making profession in your monastery, to depart from it without his abbot’s permission, except for the sake of a stricter religious life; and let no one dare retain a departing brother without letters of the community attesting the matter. In the parish churches which you possess, you may elect clerics or priests and present them to the diocesan bishop; if they are suitable, the bishop shall commit the care of souls to them, and they shall answer to him in spiritual matters but to you in temporal matters. [Col. 1367B–C]

We command that chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordinations of clerics to be promoted to sacred orders shall be supplied to you by the diocesan bishop without any impropriety. When, however, a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, it shall be lawful for you, with doors shut, excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded, bells not rung, and in a subdued voice, to celebrate the divine offices. We also decree that the burial-place of that institution shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last wishes of those who resolve to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while preserving nevertheless the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. We also forbid any archbishop or bishop, [Col. 1367D] or their official, to presume, without a manifest and reasonable cause, to pronounce against you or your church a sentence of excommunication, suspension, or interdict, or to impose new or unlawful exactions. Moreover, we hold valid the liberties, immunities, and reasonable customs hitherto observed in your church, and we will that they remain inviolate in future times.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved whole and intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. [Col. 1368A]

If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark, subscribe, etc.

Given at Verona through the hand of Hugh, notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Nones of September [3 September], in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1185, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Lucius III.

## CCXLII. Privilege for the canons of the Church of Épinal. (Verona, October 17.)

*[D. Calmet, History of Lorraine, II, Proofs, p. 390.]*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the Church of Épinal: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The most holy Roman Church is accustomed, by the duty of its habitual piety, to love its devoted and humble sons more warmly and, like a loving mother, to cherish them with the protection of her safeguard lest they be troubled by the molestations of wicked men. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, considering the devotion which we know you bear toward blessed Peter and ourselves, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the protection of this present writing, the aforesaid church of ours in which, under the care of our venerable brother B. [Bertrann], bishop of Metz, you are devoted to divine service. We establish that it shall be lawful for you to receive for conversion persons fleeing the world, free and absolved, [Col. 1368B–C] and retain them without any opposition. We decree also that the burial-place of that institution shall be free, and that no one may oppose the devotion and last wishes of those who resolve to be buried there, unless perhaps they are excommunicated or under interdict, while preserving nevertheless the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. Further, by apostolic authority we forbid the diocesan bishop to compel you to attend his synod unless you possess a church in his diocese, or such offences appear among you that your dean can neither correct nor ought to correct.

Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our protection, ordinance, and prohibition, or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. [Col. 1368D]

Given at Verona, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of November [16 October].

## CCXLIII. Privilege for the Church of Belluno. (Verona, October 18.)

*[Ughelli, Italia sacra, V, 153.]*

LUCIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GERARD, bishop-elect of the Church of Belluno, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made of us which is judged consonant with religion and honour, it is fitting that we grant it with willing mind and afford fitting assistance to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the power of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the Church of Belluno, over which, by God’s favour, you are known to preside. First, we establish that no layman may extort tithes from you or your successors from the lands which you cultivate in your own diocese or that of Ceneda, or from the produce of animals. We also grant that you shall possess the tithes of newly cleared land in your bishopric and in the district of Oderzo which cultivators cultivate by your labour or at your expense. Furthermore, we forbid anyone, against your will, to receive or retain servants of your church. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods you now lawfully and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire by reasonable means with God’s favour, shall remain firm and inviolate to you and your successors. Of these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: [Col. 1369A–B]

The parish church of St. Peter of Mussolento, with its chapels, castle, and appurtenances, both spiritual and temporal. The parish church of St. Gregory with its chapels; the chapel of St. Peter of Tuba; the chapel of the Holy Cross; the city, with its court and lordship, both spiritual and temporal, and with Anta, which lies beside the city. The castle of Castello, with its parish church, chapels, court, and appurtenances [Col. 1369C]; the castle of Medone; the castle of Agordo, with its county, the mountain of Falcata, and its other appurtenances. One half of the castle of Zumelle; the right of appointment which you possess in the chapel of that castle and in its court; the castle of St. George with its appurtenances. The parish church of Cadola with its chapels. The bridge of Polpet, with its bank and tolls. The parish church of St. Mary of Alpago with its chapels, and the county with the two tithes which are in that same county. The castle of Pucenigo, with the county bounded by the summit of Mount Pietra Cisa, by the mountain called the Iron Cross, by the summit of Mount Cavallo, by Campo Sillio within the same boundaries, and by the woodland with its tithes and appurtenances.
